14Then the LORD said to me, “Lies are what the prophets prophesy in my name. I did not send them, I gave them no command, and I did not speak to them. What they prophesy to you is a false vision, divination, worthless things and the deceit of their own hearts.

15Therefore the LORD says this about the prophets who prophesy in my name although I did not send them, and who say, ‘Sword and famine will not come on this land’: Those prophets will come to their end by sword and famine. 16The people who hear their prophecies will be flung into the streets of Jerusalem by famine and sword, and no one will bury them, nor their wives, their sons and their daughters. I will pour their own evil out upon them.
17Say this word to them:
‘Let tears stream from my eyes night and day, and let them not stop,
for the virgin, my dear people, has been broken by a great blow,
a wound that is very severe.
18If I go out to the open fields, there lie those slain by the sword;
if I enter the city,
there are those sick from famine.
Even prophet and priest go roaming off to a land they do not know.’”

Have you rejected Judah?

19Have you rejected Judah altogether?
Has Zion become hateful to you?
Why have you struck us down beyond any healing?
We hoped for peace, but nothing good came;
for a time of healing, but there was only terror.
20LORD, we know our wickedness and the guilt of our ancestors;
we have sinned against you.
21Do not treat us with scorn, for the sake of your name;
do not bring shame on the throne of your glory.
Remember, and do not break your covenant with us.
22Is there any among the empty idols of the nations that can make it rain?
Can the heavens give showers on their own?
Is it not you, LORD our God? We wait in hope for you,
for it is you who made all these things.
fields.summary: During a drought Jeremiah pleads for the people, but God forbids him to pray for them and condemns the prophets who promise peace.

fields.title: Jeremiah 15
fields.body_html:
Not even Moses and Samuel

1Then the LORD said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me to plead for them, my heart would not go out to this people. Send them away from my presence; let them leave! 2And when they ask you, ‘Where are we to go?’ tell them, ‘The LORD says this: Whoever is marked out for death, to death; whoever is marked out for the sword, to the sword; whoever is marked out for famine, to famine; and whoever is marked out for captivity, to captivity.’ 3Over them I will set four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, dogs to drag them off, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy. 4Because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and what he did in Jerusalem, I will make them a horror to every kingdom on earth.”
5Who will take pity on you, Jerusalem?
Who will grieve over you?
Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
6You have rejected me, declares the LORD; you keep turning your back.
So I have reached out my hand against you and destroyed you;
I am tired of relenting.
7With a winnowing fork I have scattered them at the gates of the land.
I have taken their children and destroyed my people,
because they did not turn from their ways.
8Before me their widows have become more than the sand of the seas.
At noon I have brought a destroyer against them, against the mothers of young men;
I have made anguish and terror fall on them suddenly.
9The mother of seven grows faint and gasps out her life; her sun has set while it is still day; she is shamed and humiliated.
And those of them who remain I will give to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD.

Woe is me, my mother

10Woe is me, my mother,
that you gave birth to me, a man the whole land strives and quarrels with!
I have not lent money, and no one has lent money to me, yet every one of them curses me.

11The LORD said:
I will surely set you free for your good;
I will surely make your enemy come to you pleading in the time of disaster, in the time of distress.
12Can anyone smash iron, iron from the north, or bronze?
13Your wealth and your treasures I will hand over as plunder, free of charge,
because of all your sins throughout your territory.
14I will make you go with your enemies into a land you do not know,
for a fire has been lit by my anger, and it will burn against you.

15You know, LORD; remember me and come to my aid, and avenge me on those who hunt me down.
Do not be so patient with them that I am swept away.
Know that it is for your sake that I suffer insults.
16Your words were found, and I fed on them;
your word became a joy to me and gladness to my heart,
because your name has been called over me, LORD God of Armies.

17I never sat in the circle of revelers or celebrated with them;
with your hand on me I sat by myself,
because you had filled me with indignation.

18Why is my pain endless and my wound beyond cure?
It will not heal.
Will you truly be to me like a stream that deceives,
like waters that cannot be trusted?

If you return

19So the LORD says this: If you turn back, I will take you back, and you will stand before me.
If you bring out what is precious and not what is worthless, you will be as my mouth.
They may turn to you,
but you are not to turn to them.
20I will make you a fortified wall of bronze facing this people;
they will make war on you, but they will not overcome you,
for I am with you to save you and to rescue you, declares the LORD.
21I will rescue you from the power of the wicked
and ransom you from the grip of the ruthless.
fields.summary: Even Moses and Samuel could not turn God’s heart toward this people. Jeremiah laments his calling, and God promises to make him a wall of bronze if he returns.

fields.title: Jeremiah 16
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah is not to marry

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2“Do not marry, and do not have sons or daughters in this place. 3For the LORD says this about the sons and daughters who are born in this place, about the mothers who give birth to them, and about the fathers who bring them into the world in this land: 4They will die of wasting diseases. No one will mourn them or bury them; they will lie like dung on the surface of the ground. Sword and famine will finish them off, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and for the wild animals.

5For the LORD says this: Do not go into a house where a funeral meal is being held. Do not go there to mourn or to show them sympathy, for I have withdrawn my peace from this people, declares the LORD, my loyal love and my compassion. 6Great and small alike will die in this land. They will not be buried, no one will mourn for them, and no one will gash their body or shave their head for them. 7No one will break bread for the mourners to comfort them for the dead, and no one will give them the cup of consolation to drink for a father or a mother. 8And do not go into a house where there is feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.

9For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Before your eyes and in your own lifetime, I am going to silence in this place the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride. 10When you report all these words to this people, they will ask you, ‘Why has the LORD announced this whole great disaster against us? What is our guilt, and what sin have we committed against the LORD our God?’ 11Then you are to say to them, ‘It is because your ancestors abandoned me, declares the LORD. They followed other gods, served them and bowed down to them. They abandoned me and did not keep my instruction. 12And you yourselves have behaved even worse than your ancestors. Look, each of you follows the stubbornness of your own evil heart and refuses to listen to me. 13So I will hurl you out of this land into a land unknown to you and to your ancestors. There you will serve other gods by day and by night, because I will show you no favor.’

Brought back from the north

14Therefore, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up the Israelites from the land of Egypt,’ 15but, ‘As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up the Israelites from the land of the north and from all the lands where he had driven them.’ I will bring them back to their own land, which I gave to their ancestors.

16Look, I am about to summon many fishermen, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. Then afterward I will summon many hunters, and they will hunt them down from every mountain, every hill and the cracks in the rocks. 17For my eyes are on every path they take. They are not hidden from me, and their guilt is not concealed from my sight. 18First I will repay them double for their guilt and their sin, because they have defiled my land with the lifeless corpses of their detestable idols and filled my inheritance with their abominations.”

The nations will come

19LORD, my strength, my fortress, my refuge on the day of trouble,
to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth
and say, “Our ancestors inherited nothing but lies,
worthless idols that did them no good at all.”
20Can people make gods for themselves?
Such things are not gods at all!
21Therefore I am going to teach them;
this time I will make my power and my might known to them,
and they will know that my name is the LORD.
fields.summary: Jeremiah must not marry or join in feasting or mourning, as a sign of coming disaster. God will one day bring the people back from all the lands.

fields.title: Jeremiah 17
fields.body_html:
Sin engraved with iron

1Judah’s sin is written down with an iron stylus, with a diamond point;
it is engraved on the tablet of their hearts
and on the horns of your altars,
2while their children remember their altars
and their Asherah poles beside the green trees
on the high hills.
3My mountain in the open country, I will hand over your wealth and all your treasures as plunder,
along with your high places, because of the sin committed throughout your territory.
4Through your own doing you will let go of the inheritance I gave you,
and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know;
for you have set my anger burning like a fire that will burn forever.

Cursed and blessed

5The LORD says this: Cursed is the one who puts trust in human beings
and leans on mere flesh for strength,
whose heart turns away from the LORD.
6They will be like a bare shrub in the desert,
and will not see good when it comes.
They will live in the scorched places of the wilderness,
in a salt land where no one lives.

7Blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD,
whose confidence rests in the LORD.
8They will be like a tree set out beside the water, that sends its roots out along a stream.
It has no fear when the heat comes;
its leaves stay green.
In a year of drought it has no worries,
and it never stops bearing fruit.
9The heart is more devious than anything else, and it is past healing;
who can understand it?
10I, the LORD, search the heart and test the inner feelings,
to give each person what their ways deserve,
what the fruit of their deeds has earned.

11Like a partridge that sits on eggs it never laid
is the one who gets rich by unjust means;
halfway through life the riches will leave them,
and in the end they will be shown a fool.
12A glorious throne, raised high from the very beginning,
is the place where our sanctuary stands.
13LORD, Hope of Israel,
all who desert you will be put to shame.
Those who turn from me will have their names written in the dust,
because they have deserted the LORD, the spring of living water.

14Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed;
rescue me, and I will be safe;
for you are the one I praise.
15See how they taunt me:
“Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come true, then!”
16But I have not run away from being a shepherd who follows you; I have not longed for the day of disaster, and you know it.
Every word that left my lips was spoken openly before you.
17Do not become a terror to me;
you are my refuge on the day of disaster.
18Let those who hunt me down be put to shame, but do not let me be shamed;
let them be shattered with fear,
but do not let me be shattered.
Bring the day of disaster on them,
and crush them twice over.

Carrying loads on the Sabbath

19The LORD said this to me: “Go and take your stand in the People’s Gate, the gate the kings of Judah use when they enter and leave, and then in all the gates of Jerusalem. 20Say to them: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah, all Judah, and everyone living in Jerusalem who comes in through these gates.

21The LORD says this: Be on your guard, for your lives depend on it. Do not carry any load on the Sabbath day or bring it in through the gates of Jerusalem. 22Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work at all. Set the Sabbath day apart as holy, just as I commanded your ancestors. 23But they did not listen or pay attention. They made their necks stiff so they would not hear or accept correction. 24But if you truly listen to me, declares the LORD, and bring no load in through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keep the Sabbath day holy and do no work on it, 25then kings and officials who sit on David’s throne will come in through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their officials, along with the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem. And this city will be lived in forever. 26People will come in from the towns of Judah and the places surrounding Jerusalem, from Benjamin’s territory and the western foothills, from the hill country and the Negev. They will bring burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and they will bring offerings of thanks to the house of the LORD. 27But if you do not listen to me and keep the Sabbath day holy, if you carry loads as you come in through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set fire to its gates, a fire that will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem and will not be put out.’”
fields.summary: Judah’s sin is written on their hearts with an iron pen. The heart is more devious than anything else, and those who trust in people are cursed, but those who trust God are like a tree planted by water.

fields.title: Jeremiah 18
fields.body_html:
Clay in the potter’s hand

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: 2“Get up and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will let you hear my words.” 3So I went down to the potter’s house, and there he was, working at the wheel. 4If the pot he was shaping from the clay went wrong in the potter’s hand, he would make it over into another pot, whatever seemed best to him.

5Then the word of the LORD came to me: 6“House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares the LORD. As the clay is in the potter’s hand, so you are in my hand, house of Israel.

7At one time I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, that I will uproot it, tear it down and destroy it, 8but that nation I have spoken against turns from its evil, then I will relent and not bring on it the disaster I had planned.

9And at another time I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, that I will build it and plant it, 10but it does what is evil in my sight and does not obey me, then I will relent and not do the good I had promised it.

11So now, say to the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem, ‘The LORD says this: I am shaping disaster for you and making plans against you. Turn back, every one of you, from your evil way, and change your ways and your actions for the better.’ 12But they will say, ‘It is no use! We will follow our own plans; each of us will act in the stubbornness of our evil hearts.’”

13Therefore the LORD says this:
Ask among the nations,
who has ever heard of such things?
The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.
14Does the snow of Lebanon ever vanish from its rocky heights?
Are the cold streams that flow from far away ever cut off?
15Yet my people have forgotten me; they make offerings of incense to worthless gods,
which have made them stumble in their ways, on the ancient roads,
so that they walk on side paths, on a road that is not built up,
16making their land a horror, an object of scorn forever;
all who pass by it will be appalled and shake their heads.
17Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy;
I will show them my back, not my face, on the day of their disaster.

A plot against Jeremiah

18Then they said, “Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah. Instruction will never be lost to the priest, or counsel to the wise, or the word to the prophet. Come, let us attack him with words and pay no attention to anything he says.”
19Pay attention to me, LORD,
and hear what my accusers are saying.
20Is evil the right return for good?
Yet they have dug a pit to take my life.
Remember how I stood before you and spoke up for their good,
to turn your wrath away from them.
21So hand their children over to famine;
give them up to the power of the sword.
Let their wives be left childless and widowed,
their men be killed by plague,
and their young men be struck down by the sword in battle.
22Let screams ring out from their houses
when you bring raiders on them without warning,
for they have dug a pit to catch me
and hidden traps for my feet.
23But you, LORD, know all their plans to kill me.
Do not forgive their guilt
or wipe out their sin from your sight.
Let them be brought down before you;
act against them in the time of your anger.
fields.summary: At the potter’s house God shows Jeremiah that God can reshape Israel as the potter reshapes the clay. The people plot against Jeremiah.

fields.title: Jeremiah 19
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah breaks a flask

1The LORD said this: “Go and buy a clay flask from a potter. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests, 2and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, by the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words I tell you. 3Say: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to bring such disaster on this place that it will make the ears of all who hear of it tingle, 4because they have forsaken me and made this place belong to foreign gods. They have burned incense in it to other gods, gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah had ever known, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent. 5They have built Baal’s high places to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal, a thing I never commanded or spoke of, and that never entered my mind.

6So look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer call this place Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom; they will call it the Valley of Slaughter. 7In this place I will empty out the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will have them cut down by the sword in front of their enemies, by the hand of those who want to kill them, and I will give their dead bodies as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals. 8I will make this city a horror and an object of scorn. Everyone who passes by will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all its wounds. 9I will make them eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters, and they will eat each other’s flesh during the siege, in the distress that their enemies and those who want to kill them bring upon them.’ 10Then break the flask while the men who went with you watch, 11and say to them: ‘The LORD of Armies says this: In the same way I will break this people and this city, as a potter’s jar is broken that can never be mended. They will bury the dead in Topheth because there will be no other place left to bury them. 12This is what I will do to this place and to the people who live here, declares the LORD: I will make this city like Topheth. 13The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of Judah’s kings will be unclean like the place of Topheth: all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to the whole host of heaven, and poured drink offerings out to other gods.’”

14Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy. He took his stand in the court of the LORD’s house and spoke to all the people:

15“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to bring on this city and all its towns all the disaster I have announced against it, because they have stiffened their necks and refused to listen to my words.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah breaks a clay jar in the Valley of Ben-hinnom as a sign that God will smash Jerusalem.

fields.title: Jeremiah 20
fields.body_html:
Pashhur puts Jeremiah in the stocks

1Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was the chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things. 2Pashhur beat Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the upper Benjamin Gate of the house of the LORD. 3The next day, when Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks, Jeremiah told him, “Pashhur is not the name the LORD gives you. His name for you is Terror on Every Side.

4For the LORD says this: ‘I am about to turn you into a terror to yourself and to everyone who loves you. Before your own eyes they will fall by the swords of their enemies. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon. He will carry them away to Babylon as exiles and put them to the sword. 5I will hand over to their enemies all the wealth stored up in this city, all that its people have worked for, all its valuable things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will loot them, seize them and haul them away to Babylon. 6As for you, Pashhur, you and everyone in your household will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and you will die and be buried there, together with all the friends to whom you have prophesied lies.’”

Like a fire in my bones

7You enticed me, LORD, and I was taken in;
you were too strong for me, and you won.
All day long people laugh at me;
every one of them makes fun of me.
8Whenever I speak, I cry out;
I shout, “Violence and ruin!”
So the word of the LORD has brought me insult and scorn all day long.
9If I say, “I will not mention him or speak in his name anymore,”
then it is like a fire burning in my heart,
shut up inside my bones.
I wear myself out holding it in, and I cannot.
10I hear many whispering, “Terror on every side!
Inform on him! Let us inform on him!”
All my trusted friends
watch for me to stumble:
“Perhaps he can be enticed; then we will get the better of him
and take our revenge on him.”
11But the LORD is with me like a terrifying warrior;
so those who hunt me will stumble and will not win.
They will be thoroughly shamed when they fail,
with a lasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
12LORD of Armies, you who test the righteous,
who see the inner feelings and the mind,
let me see you take vengeance on them,
for I have laid my case before you.

13Sing to the LORD!
Praise the LORD!
For he has rescued the poor from the power of those who do evil.

Why was I born?

14A curse on the day I was born!
May the day my mother gave birth to me never be blessed!
15A curse on the man who brought my father the news,
“You have a son, a boy!”
and made him so very glad.
16May that man be like the cities
that the LORD overthrew, never relenting;
may he hear a cry of distress in the morning
and the alarm of battle at noon,
17because he did not kill me in the womb;
then my mother would have been my grave,
her womb pregnant for all time.
18Why did I ever come out of the womb
to look on hardship and grief,
and to have my days run out in shame?
fields.summary: Pashhur the priest beats Jeremiah and puts him in the stocks. Jeremiah complains that God has deceived him, yet God’s word is like a fire shut up in his bones, and he curses the day he was born.

fields.title: Jeremiah 21
fields.body_html:
Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD at the time King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah the priest, son of Maaseiah, to him with this request: 2“Please seek the LORD on our behalf, because Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon is at war with us. Perhaps the LORD will do for us one of his wonders, as in all the wonders of the past, so that the king will lift the siege and leave us.”

3Jeremiah answered them, “Tell Zedekiah this: 4‘The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to turn back the weapons of war in your hands, the weapons you are using to fight the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you from outside the wall. I will gather them into the heart of this city. 5I myself will fight against you with my hand stretched out and with my strong arm, in anger, in fury and in great rage. 6I will strike down those who live in this city, people and animals alike; they will die of a terrible plague. 7Afterward, declares the LORD, I will hand over King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials and the people, all in this city who survive the plague, the sword and the famine, to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies, to those who want them dead. He will put them to the sword; he will show them no pity, no mercy and no compassion.’” 8“And say to this people, ‘The LORD says this: Look, I am putting in front of you the way that leads to life and the way that leads to death. 9Those who stay in this city will die by sword, famine and plague. But those who go out and surrender to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live; they will come away with their lives as their only plunder. 10For I have set my face against this city for disaster and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.’”

To the royal house of Judah

11To the royal house of Judah:
Hear the word of the LORD.
12House of David, the LORD says this:
Give fair judgment every morning,
and rescue the one who has been robbed from the power of the oppressor.
Otherwise my fury will break out like fire and burn with no one to put it out,
because of your evil deeds.
13Look, I am against you, you who sit above the valley, rock on the plain, declares the LORD,
you who say, “Who can come down on us?
Who can break into our homes?”
14I will punish you as your actions have earned, declares the LORD.
I will set fire to her forest,
and it will consume everything around her.
fields.summary: When Zedekiah asks for God’s help against Babylon, Jeremiah answers that God will fight against Jerusalem. Those who surrender to the Babylonians will live.

fields.title: Jeremiah 22
fields.body_html:
A word for the palace of Judah

1The LORD says this: “Go down to the palace of Judah’s king and speak this message there. 2Say: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David’s throne, you and your officials and your people who come in through these gates.

3The LORD says this: Practice justice and righteousness. Rescue anyone who has been robbed from the power of the oppressor. Do not mistreat the outsider, the orphan or the widow, do not use violence against them, and do not shed innocent blood in this place. 4For if you are careful to do what this word commands, then kings who sit on David’s throne will come in through the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, each with his officials and his people. 5But if you will not listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that this palace will become a ruin.’”

6For the LORD says this about the palace of the king of Judah:
To me you are like Gilead, like the heights of Lebanon,
but I will surely make you a wilderness,
like towns where no one lives.
7I will appoint destroyers against you, each with his weapons.
They will cut down your finest cedars
and throw them into the fire.
8People of many nations will pass by this city and say to one another, “Why has the LORD treated this great city like this?” 9And the answer will be, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and worshiped other gods and served them.”

Shallum will not return

10Do not weep for the one who is dead;
do not mourn for him.
Weep and keep weeping for the one who is going away,
because he will never return
or see his homeland again.

11For the LORD says this about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who became king in place of his father Josiah and has gone away from this place: He will never come back here. 12He will die in the place where they have taken him as a captive, and he will never see this land again.

A palace built by injustice

13Woe to the man who builds his palace without righteousness
and his upper rooms without justice,
who makes his fellow citizens work for nothing
and does not pay them their wages.
14He says, “I will build myself a huge palace
with spacious upper rooms.”
He cuts windows into it,
panels it with cedar and paints it with vermilion.
15Does it make you a king to outdo others in cedar?
Did not your father eat and drink
and also do justice and righteousness?
Then all went well with him.
16He defended the cause of the poor and the needy, and then all was well.
Is that not what it means to know me? declares the LORD.
17But your eyes and your heart are set on nothing
but dishonest gain,
on shedding innocent blood,
and on practicing oppression and extortion.

18Therefore the LORD says this about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
No one will mourn for him, crying,
“Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!”
No one will mourn for him, crying,
“Alas, my master! Alas, his majesty!”
19He will be buried the way a donkey is buried,
dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

20Climb up to Lebanon and cry out;
let your voice be heard in Bashan;
cry out from the Abarim mountains,
for all your lovers have been crushed.
21I spoke to you while you felt secure,
but you said, “I will not listen.”
Ever since you were young you have behaved like this:
you have not obeyed my voice.
22The wind will herd away all your shepherds,
and your lovers will be carried into captivity.
Then you will feel shame and disgrace
because of all your wickedness.
23You who live in Lebanon,
nesting among the cedars,
how you will groan when the pains come on you,
pain like a woman in labor!
24As surely as I live, declares the LORD: Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, even if you were the signet ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off. 25I will hand you over to those who want to kill you, to those you fear, to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans. 26I will throw you and the mother who gave birth to you into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you will both die. 27They will long to return to this land, but they will never come back to it.

28Is this man Coniah a worthless, broken pot,
a jar that no one wants?
Why have he and his children been hurled out
and thrown into a land they do not know?
29Land, land, land,
hear the word of the LORD!

30The LORD says this: Record this man as childless,
a man who will not succeed in his lifetime,
for none of his descendants will succeed in sitting on the throne of David
or ruling again in Judah.
fields.summary: Jeremiah tells the kings of Judah to do justice and warns them of judgment. He pronounces judgment on Shallum, Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin.

fields.title: Jeremiah 23
fields.body_html:
Shepherds who scatter the flock

1Woe to the shepherds who are destroying and scattering the sheep of my pasture, declares the LORD. 2So the LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the shepherds who shepherd my people: You have scattered my flock and chased them off, and you have not looked after them. So now I will look after you, and punish the evil you have done, declares the LORD. 3I myself will gather together the remnant of my flock from every country to which I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their grazing land, and they will be fruitful and increase. 4I will set shepherds over them who will truly tend them. They will no longer be afraid or terrified, and not one of them will be lost, declares the LORD.

A Branch for David

5The days are coming, declares the LORD,
when I will raise a righteous Branch for David.
He will reign as king and rule with wisdom,
and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
6In his days Judah will be saved,
and Israel will live in safety.
And this is the name people will give him: “The LORD Is Our Righteousness.”

7Therefore, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, “As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up the Israelites from the land of Egypt,” 8but, “As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up and led the descendants of the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them.” Then they will live in their own land.

Concerning the prophets

9Concerning the prophets:
My heart is crushed inside me, and all my bones are shaking.
I am like a drunk man,
like someone overpowered by wine,
because of the LORD and because of his holy words.
10The land is full of adulterers.
The land mourns under the curse,
and the wilderness pastures have withered.
They run their race toward evil,
and they use their power for what is wrong.
11For both prophet and priest are godless;
even in my own house I have found their wickedness, declares the LORD.
12So their path will become like slippery ground in the dark;
they will be pushed down, and there they will fall.
For I will bring disaster on them in the year I punish them, declares the LORD.
13Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something repulsive:
they prophesied by Baal
and led my people Israel astray.

14But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible:
they commit adultery and live by lies.
They strengthen the hands of those who do evil, so that no one turns away from wickedness.
To me they have all become like Sodom,
and the people of the city like Gomorrah.

15So the LORD of Armies says this about the prophets:
I am going to feed them bitter wormwood
and give them poisoned water to drink,
because from the prophets of Jerusalem
godlessness has spread through the whole land.

16The LORD of Armies says this: Do not listen to what the prophets are prophesying to you;
they are filling you with empty hopes.
They speak visions that come from their own minds,
and not from the mouth of the LORD.
17They keep telling those who despise me, “The LORD says you will have peace.”
And to all who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts they say, “No disaster will come on you.”
18For who has stood in the council of the LORD
to see and to hear his word?
Who has listened closely to his word and heard it?

19Look, the storm of the LORD! Fury has burst out,
a whirlwind spinning around;
it will crash down on the heads of the wicked.
20The anger of the LORD will not turn away
until he has fully carried out what he has purposed in his heart.
In the days ahead
you will understand it fully.
21I did not send these prophets, but they ran anyway.
I did not speak to them, but they prophesied all the same.
22But if they had stood in my council,
they would have announced my words to my people
and turned them from their evil path
and from their wicked deeds.

23Am I a God who is only near, declares the LORD,
and not a God who is far away?
24Can anyone hide in secret places where I cannot see them? declares the LORD.
Do I not fill heaven and earth? declares the LORD.
25I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in my name. They say, “I had a dream! I had a dream!” 26How long will this go on in the hearts of the prophets who prophesy lies, who prophesy the deceit of their own minds, 27who plan to make my people forget my name with the dreams they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot my name because of Baal? 28Let the prophet who has a dream tell it as a dream, but let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain? declares the LORD. 29Is not my word like fire, declares the LORD, like a hammer that smashes rock to pieces?

30So I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who steal my words from one another. 31I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who speak with their own tongues and then announce, “The LORD declares.” 32I am against those who prophesy false dreams, declares the LORD. They tell them and lead my people astray with their lies and their reckless boasting, though I did not send them or give them any command. They do this people no good at all, declares the LORD. 33When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, “What is the LORD’s burden?” you are to say to them, “What burden? I will throw you off, declares the LORD.” 34If a prophet or a priest or anyone else says, “The LORD’s burden,” I will punish that person and their household. 35This is what each of you is to say to your friends and relatives: “What has the LORD answered?” or “What has the LORD said?” 36But you must never again speak of “the LORD’s burden,” because each person’s own word will become their burden, and you twist the words of the living God, the LORD of Armies, our God. 37This is how you are to speak to a prophet: “What answer has the LORD given you?” or “What has the LORD said?” 38But if you do say, “The LORD’s burden,” then the LORD says this: Because you have used these words, “The LORD’s burden,” even though I sent word to you and said, “Do not say, ‘The LORD’s burden,’” 39therefore I will forget you completely and throw you away from my presence, you and the city I gave to you and your ancestors, 40and I will make you a disgrace for all time, an everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.
fields.summary: God will judge the shepherds who scatter the flock and will raise up a righteous Branch for David. God condemns the lying prophets who speak their own dreams.

fields.title: Jeremiah 24
fields.body_html:
Two baskets set before the temple

1The LORD showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had taken Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem, together with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen and the smiths, and had brought them to Babylon. 2One basket held very good figs, like figs that ripen first; the other basket held very bad figs, so bad that they could not be eaten.

3Then the LORD asked me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad that they cannot be eaten.”

4Then the word of the LORD came to me: 5“The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Like these good figs, so I will regard with favor the exiles from Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans. 6I will keep my eyes on them for their good and bring them back to this land. I will build them, not tear them down; I will plant them, not uproot them. 7I will give them a heart to know me, to know that I am the LORD; and they will be my people, and I will be their God, because they will turn back to me with their whole heart.

8But as for the bad figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten, the LORD says this: In the same way I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the rest of Jerusalem who are left in this land, and those who are living in the land of Egypt. 9I will make them a horror and a disaster to all the kingdoms of the earth. In all the places where I drive them, they will be a disgrace and a proverb, a byword and a curse. 10I will send sword, famine and plague against them until they are wiped out from the land I gave to them and to their ancestors.”
fields.summary: God shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs: the good figs are the exiles God will bring back, and the bad figs are those who stay in Jerusalem.

fields.title: Jeremiah 25
fields.body_html:
Twenty-three years of warnings

1This message came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in what was also the first year of the reign of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. 2Jeremiah the prophet spoke it to all the people of Judah and to everyone living in Jerusalem. He said: 3“For twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, up to this very day, the word of the LORD has come to me. Again and again I have spoken to you, but you have not listened. 4And the LORD has sent you all his servants the prophets again and again, but you have not listened or even paid attention. 5They said, ‘Turn back, every one of you, from your evil ways and your evil deeds, and you will live in the land that the LORD gave to you and your ancestors to keep for all time. 6Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them. Do not make me angry with the idols your hands have made, and I will not harm you.’ 7But you have not listened to me, declares the LORD. You have made me angry with the idols your hands have made, and brought harm on yourselves.

8So the LORD of Armies says this: Because you have not listened to my words, 9I am going to send for all the peoples of the north, declares the LORD, and for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I will bring them against this land and its people and against all the nations around it. I will devote them to destruction and make them a horror, an object of scorn, and ruins forever. 10I will take away from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, the grinding of the millstones and the light of the lamp. 11This whole land will become a desolate ruin, and for seventy years these nations will serve the king of Babylon. 12But when the seventy years are over, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt, declares the LORD. I will punish the land of the Chaldeans and make it a desolation forever. 13I will bring on that land everything I have said against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations. 14For many nations and great kings will make them serve in their turn, and I will repay them for what they have done, for the work of their hands.”

The cup of wine

15For the LORD, the God of Israel, said this to me: “Take this cup filled with the wine of my wrath from my hand, and make all the nations I am sending you to drink it. 16When they drink, they will stagger and lose their minds because of the sword I am sending among them.” 17So I took the cup from the hand of the LORD and made all the nations drink it to whom the LORD had sent me: 18Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, an object of scorn and a curse, as they are today; 19Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people, 20all the foreign peoples there; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines, of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and what is left of Ashdod; 21Edom, Moab and the Ammonites, 22all the kings of Tyre and all the kings of Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea; 23Dedan, Tema and Buz, and all who clip the hair at their temples; 24all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the desert; 25all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media; 26and all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach will drink. 27“Then say to them, ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Drink and get drunk and vomit; fall down and do not get up again, because of the sword I am sending among you.’ 28If they will not take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them, ‘The LORD of Armies says this: You must drink it! 29For see, I am starting to bring disaster on the city that bears my name. Do you really think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am calling for a sword against everyone who lives on the earth, declares the LORD of Armies.’
30As for you, prophesy all these words against them. Tell them:
‘The LORD roars from on high;
from his holy dwelling he raises his voice.
He roars and roars against his own pasture;
he shouts like those who tread the grapes,
a shout against all who live on the earth.
31The uproar reaches to the end of the earth,
for the LORD has a case against the nations.
He is bringing all humankind to judgment,
and he hands the wicked over to the sword, declares the LORD.

Disaster spreads to the nations

32The LORD of Armies says this:
Look! Disaster is spreading from nation to nation,
and a great storm is rising
from the far ends of the earth.
33On that day those slain by the LORD will lie
from one end of the earth to the other.
No one will mourn them or gather them or bury them;
they will be like dung lying on the ground.
34Wail, you shepherds! Cry out!
Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock!
The time has come for you to be slaughtered and scattered,
and you will fall and break like a precious jar.
35The shepherds will have nowhere to flee,
the leaders of the flock no way to escape.
36Listen to the shepherds crying out,
the leaders of the flock wailing,
for the LORD is laying waste their pasture.
37The peaceful meadows lie in ruins
because of the fierce anger of the LORD.
38Like a lion he has left his den,
and their land has become a desolate waste
because of the fury of the oppressor
and because of his fierce anger.’”
fields.summary: Because Judah has not listened for twenty-three years, Babylon will rule them for seventy years. The nations must drink the cup of God’s wrath.

fields.title: Jeremiah 26
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah’s sermon in the temple

1Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came from the LORD: 2“The LORD says this: Take your stand in the courtyard of the LORD’s house and speak to the people of all the towns of Judah who come to worship at the house of the LORD. Tell them all the words I have commanded you to speak to them; do not hold back a single word. 3Perhaps they will listen and each one will turn from his evil way. Then I will relent concerning the disaster I am planning to bring on them because of their evil deeds. 4Say to them, ‘The LORD says this: If you will not listen to me and walk in my instruction, which I have set before you, 5and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, the ones I send you again and again, though you have not listened, 6then I will make this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make a curse word for all the nations of the earth.’”

Jeremiah on trial for his life

7The priests, the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of the LORD. 8As soon as Jeremiah finished saying everything the LORD had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets and all the people seized him and said, “You must die! 9Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD that this house will be like Shiloh and this city will lie in ruins with no one living in it?” And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD. 10The officials of Judah heard about these things, and they came up from the royal palace to the house of the LORD and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.

11Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, “This man ought to be condemned to death. He has prophesied against this city; you heard it with your own ears.” 12Then Jeremiah addressed all the officials and all the people: “It was the LORD who sent me to prophesy against this house and this city, to speak all the words you have heard. 13So now, change your ways and your actions for the better, and obey the voice of the LORD your God. Then the LORD will relent concerning the disaster he has pronounced against you. 14As for me, look, I am in your power. Do to me what seems good and right in your eyes. 15But know this for certain: if you put me to death, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood on yourselves, on this city and on the people who live in it, for it is true that the LORD sent me to you to speak all these words for you to hear.”

The officials refuse to condemn Jeremiah

16Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, “This man ought not to be condemned to death, for it is in the name of the LORD our God that he has spoken to us.” 17Then some of the elders of the land stood up and spoke to the whole assembly of the people:
18“Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, ‘The LORD of Armies says this:
Zion will be plowed as a field,
Jerusalem will be a mound of ruins,
and the mountain of the temple a wooded height.’
19Did Hezekiah king of Judah, or all Judah with him, put him to death? Did Hezekiah not fear the LORD and plead for the LORD’s favor, so that the LORD relented concerning the disaster he had pronounced against them? We are about to bring a great disaster on ourselves!” 20Another man, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, was also prophesying in the name of the LORD. Against this city and this land he prophesied words just like Jeremiah’s. 21When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard what he said, the king tried to have him put to death. But Uriah heard of it, and he was afraid and fled to Egypt. 22But King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him went to Egypt. 23They brought Uriah back from Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his body into the burial ground of the common people. 24But Ahikam son of Shaphan stood behind Jeremiah, so Jeremiah was not given into the people’s hands to be put to death.
fields.summary: Jeremiah is tried for prophesying against the temple, but the officials spare him. The prophet Uriah is killed for the same message.

fields.title: Jeremiah 27
fields.body_html:
Bend your necks under Babylon’s yoke

1Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: 2The LORD said this to me: “Make yourself straps and yoke bars, and put them on your neck. 3Then send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, Tyre and Sidon through the envoys who have come to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem. 4Give them this charge for their masters: ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: This is what you are to say to your masters: 5It is I who made the earth, and the people and animals that live on it, by my great power and my outstretched arm, and I give it to anyone I see fit. 6Now I have handed all these lands over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I have even given him the wild animals to serve him. 7All the nations will serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land as well. Then many nations and great kings will make him serve them. 8Any nation or kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish with sword, famine and plague, declares the LORD, until I have finished it off by his hand. 9So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your fortune-tellers or your sorcerers, who keep telling you, “You will not serve the king of Babylon.” 10They are prophesying a lie to you, and it will only lead to your being taken far from your land. I will drive you out, and you will perish. 11But any nation that bows its neck to the king of Babylon’s yoke and serves him, I will leave on its own land, declares the LORD. They will farm it and live there.’” 12I said the same things to Zedekiah king of Judah: “Bow your necks to the king of Babylon’s yoke. Serve him and his people, and you will live. 13Why should you and your people die by sword, famine and plague, as the LORD has said will happen to any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon? 14Do not listen to the words of the prophets who tell you, ‘You will not serve the king of Babylon.’ They are prophesying a lie to you. 15I did not send them, declares the LORD. They are prophesying lies in my name, and the result will be that I drive you out and you perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.” 16Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people: “The LORD says this: Do not listen to what your prophets are prophesying to you: ‘The vessels of the house of the LORD will very soon be brought back from Babylon.’ They are prophesying a lie to you. 17Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and you will live. Why should this city be turned into a ruin? 18If they really are prophets and have the word of the LORD with them, they should plead with the LORD of Armies that the vessels still left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of Judah’s king and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.

19For the LORD of Armies says this concerning the pillars, the Sea, the stands and the rest of the vessels still left in this city, 20which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left behind when he took Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem into exile in Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem,

21yes, the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this about the vessels still left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of Judah’s king and in Jerusalem: 22They will be carried to Babylon, and they will stay there until the day I come for them, declares the LORD. Then I will bring them back up and return them to this place.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah wears a yoke and tells the kings to serve Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, warning against prophets who say otherwise.

fields.title: Jeremiah 28
fields.body_html:
Hananiah breaks the yoke

1In that same year, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fifth month of the fourth year, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, spoke to me. It was in the house of the LORD, with the priests and all the people looking on: 2“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon. 3Within two full years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon. 4I will also bring Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah back to this place, with every exile of Judah who went off to Babylon, declares the LORD; for I will break the king of Babylon’s yoke.” 5Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and of all the people standing there in the house of the LORD. 6The prophet Jeremiah said, “Amen! May the LORD do just that! May the LORD make the words you have prophesied come true, and bring the vessels of the house of the LORD and all the exiles back from Babylon to this place. 7But listen now to this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people. 8The prophets who came before you and me, from ancient times, prophesied war, disaster and plague against many countries and great kingdoms. 9But the prophet who prophesies peace will be known as one whom the LORD has truly sent when his word comes to pass.” 10Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke bar off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it. 11And Hananiah spoke in the presence of all the people: “The LORD says this: In just this way, within two full years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and take it off the neck of every nation.” Then the prophet Jeremiah went away.

A yoke of iron

12After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke bar off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 13“Go and tell Hananiah, ‘The LORD says this: You have broken bars of wood, but in their place you have made bars of iron. 14For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: It is a yoke of iron that I have put on the neck of all these nations, so that they serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and serve him they will. I have given him even the wild animals.’” 15Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, “Hear this, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, and yet you have made this people trust in a lie. 16Therefore the LORD says this: I am about to send you off the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have urged rebellion against the LORD.” 17And the prophet Hananiah died that same year, in the seventh month.
fields.summary: The prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah’s yoke and promises a quick return from exile. Jeremiah announces that Hananiah will die, and he dies that year.

fields.title: Jeremiah 29
fields.body_html:
A letter to the people in exile

1This is the text of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders who were left among the exiles, to the priests and the prophets, and to all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, 2after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officers, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and smiths had gone from Jerusalem into exile, 3sending it by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah. Zedekiah king of Judah had sent these two men to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:

4“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this to all the exiles whom I sent into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon: 5Build houses and settle down in them. Plant gardens and eat what they produce. 6Marry and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they in turn have sons and daughters. Increase in number there; do not decrease. 7Seek the peace of the city where I have sent you as exiles, and pray to the LORD for it, since your own peace depends on its peace.

8For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Do not let the prophets and the diviners who are among you deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you urge them to dream. 9For they are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the LORD.

10For the LORD says this: When Babylon’s seventy years have been completed, I will come to your aid. I will keep my good promise to you and bring you back to this place. 11For I know well what I have planned for you, declares the LORD. I have planned peace for you, not disaster, so as to give you a future and a hope. 12Then you will call on me; you will come and pray to me, and I will hear you. 13You will seek me and you will find me, when you search for me with all your heart. 14I will let you find me, declares the LORD. I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile. 15You have been saying, ‘The LORD has raised up prophets for us here in Babylon.’

16But the LORD says this about the king who sits on David’s throne and about all the people who live in this city, your brothers and sisters who did not go with you into exile: 17The LORD of Armies says this: I am about to send the sword, famine and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs, so bad that they cannot be eaten. 18I will pursue them with sword, famine and plague, and I will make them a horror to every kingdom on earth. Among all the nations where I have driven them, they will be a name used in curses, a thing that appalls, an object of scorn and a disgrace, 19because they have not listened to my words, declares the LORD, the words I sent them through my servants the prophets, again and again. And you did not listen either, declares the LORD. 20But you, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon, hear the word of the LORD.

21The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this about Ahab son of Kolaiah and about Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: I am about to hand them over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your eyes. 22Their fate will become a curse that all the exiles of Judah in Babylon will use: ‘May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, the men the king of Babylon roasted alive in the fire,’ 23because they have done a disgraceful thing in Israel. They have committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives and have spoken lies in my name, words I did not command them to speak. I am the one who knows it, and I am witness to it, declares the LORD.”

A message for Shemaiah

24“To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you are to say: 25‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest and to all the priests. You wrote: 26“The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, so that there would be officers in the house of the LORD to deal with any madman who sets himself up as a prophet. You should put such a man in the stocks and the neck irons. 27So why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who sets himself up as a prophet among you? 28For he has even sent word to us in Babylon, saying, ‘It will be a long time. Build houses and settle down in them. Plant gardens and eat what they produce.’”‘” 29Zephaniah the priest read this letter aloud to Jeremiah the prophet.

30Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 31“Send this message to all the exiles: ‘The LORD says this about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, although I did not send him, and has led you to trust in a lie, 32therefore the LORD says this: I am about to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. No one of his line will be left living among this people, and he will not see the good that I am going to do for my people, declares the LORD, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD.’”
fields.summary: Jeremiah writes to the exiles in Babylon to build houses, plant gardens and seek the peace of the city, for God has plans to give them a future and a hope after seventy years.

fields.title: Jeremiah 30
fields.body_html:
The exiles will come home

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: 2The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: “Write down in a book all the words I have spoken to you. 3For the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the LORD. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will possess it.”

4These are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah:
5For the LORD says this:
“We have heard a cry of panic,
of terror, and there is no peace.”
6Ask and see:
can a man give birth?
Then why do I see every man with his hands pressed to his sides like a woman in labor,
every face gone deathly pale?
7Woe! That day is great; there is no other like it.
It is a time of distress for Jacob,
yet he will be saved out of it.
8On that day, declares the LORD of Armies,
I will break his yoke from your neck and tear off your bonds,
and foreigners will no longer make him serve them.
9They will serve the LORD their God instead
and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

10So you, Jacob my servant, do not be afraid, declares the LORD; do not be dismayed, Israel.
For I will save you from a far country, and your descendants from the land where they are captives.
Jacob will come home and have quiet and rest, and no one will make him afraid.
11For I am with you to save you, declares the LORD.
I will bring to an end all the nations among whom I scattered you, but you I will not bring to an end.
I will discipline you, but justly,
and I will not let you go unpunished.

Healing for an incurable wound

12For the LORD says this: Your injury cannot be cured;
your wound is severe.
13There is no one to take up your cause, no one for your sore;
there are no remedies, no healing for you.
14All your lovers have forgotten you;
they do not care about you.
For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with the punishment of a cruel foe,
because your guilt is great
and your sins are many.
15Why cry out over your injury?
Your pain cannot be cured.
Because your guilt is great and your sins are many,
I have done these things to you.
16Yet all who devour you will be devoured,
and all your foes, every one of them, will go into captivity.
Those who plunder you will become plunder,
and all who prey on you I will hand over as prey.
17But I will restore you to health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD,
because they have called you an outcast:
“This is Zion; no one cares about her.”

18The LORD says this: I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob
and show compassion to his homes.
The city will be rebuilt on its ruin mound,
and the palace will stand where it should.
19From them will come songs of thanks and the sound of people celebrating.
I will make them many, and they will not dwindle;
I will bring them honor, and they will not be looked down on.
20Their children will be as they were long ago;
their congregation will be firmly established before me,
and I will punish all who oppress them.
21One of their own will be their leader; their ruler will come from among them.
I will bring him near, and he will come close to me,
for who would dare to risk his life by coming close to me? declares the LORD.
22So you will be my people,
and I will be your God.

23Look, the storm of the LORD! Fury has burst out,
a whirlwind sweeping on;
it will crash down on the heads of the wicked.
24The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn away
until he has fully carried out what he has purposed in his heart.
In the days ahead you will understand this.
fields.summary: God promises to restore the fortunes of Israel and Judah and bring them back to the land. Their wound is incurable, but God will heal it.

fields.title: Jeremiah 31
fields.body_html:
1At that time, declares the LORD, I will be God to every clan of Israel,
and they will be my people.

Loved with an everlasting love

2The LORD says this:
The people who escaped the sword found favor in the wilderness
as Israel went in search of rest.
3From far away the LORD appeared to me:
I have loved you with an everlasting love,
so I have kept on showing you loyal love.
4Once more I will build you, and you will be rebuilt,
Virgin Israel;
once more you will deck yourself with your tambourines
and go out in the dances of the joyful.
5Once more you will plant vineyards
on the hills of Samaria;
those who plant them will enjoy their fruit.
6For a day is coming when watchmen will call out
on the hills of Ephraim,
“Come, let us go up to Zion,
to the LORD our God!”

7For the LORD says this: Sing for joy over Jacob,
shout for the foremost of the nations.
Make it heard, give praise, and say,
“LORD, save your people,
the remnant of Israel!”
8I am going to bring them out of the northern land and gather them from the ends of the earth.
Among them will be the blind and the lame,
pregnant women and women in labor, all together.
A great assembly will return here.
9They will come weeping,
and I will lead them as they plead for mercy.
I will guide them beside streams of water,
on a level road where they will not stumble,
because I am a father to Israel,
and Ephraim is my firstborn son.

10Hear the word of the LORD, you nations;
announce it in the coastlands far away.
Say, “The one who scattered Israel will gather him
and watch over him as a shepherd watches his flock.”
11For the LORD has ransomed Jacob
and redeemed him from the power of one too strong for him.
12They will come and sing out with joy on Zion’s heights;
their faces will shine over the good gifts of the LORD, over grain, new wine and oil,
and over the young of the flocks and herds.
Their whole life will be like a watered garden,
and they will never grow faint again.
13Then the young women will rejoice in the dance,
the young men and the old men with them.
I will turn their mourning into joy;
I will comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.
14I will fill the priests with rich food in abundance,
and my people will have their fill of my good gifts, declares the LORD.

Rachel weeping for her children

15The LORD says this: In Ramah a voice is heard, mourning and bitter weeping:
Rachel weeping for her children.
She will not let anyone comfort her for her children, because they are gone.

16The LORD says this: Hold back your voice from weeping
and your eyes from tears,
for your labor will have its reward, declares the LORD;
they will come back from the land of the enemy.
17There is hope for your future, declares the LORD;
your children will come back to their own land.

18I have certainly heard Ephraim grieving:
“You disciplined me, and I took the discipline,
like a calf never trained to the yoke.
Bring me back, and I will come back,
for you are the LORD my God.
19After I turned away, I was sorry;
after I came to understand, I struck my thigh in grief.
I was ashamed and disgraced,
because I carried the shame of my youth.”
20Is Ephraim my dear son, a child who delights me?
For whenever I speak against him,
I still remember him and cannot forget.
That is why my heart aches for him;
I will surely show him compassion, declares the LORD.

21Set up road markers for yourself;
put up signposts.
Fix your mind on the highway, the road you traveled.
Come back, Virgin Israel;
come back to these towns of yours.
22How long will you waver this way and that,
you faithless daughter?
For the LORD has created something new in the land:
a woman will encircle a man.

23The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: When I restore their fortunes, people in the land of Judah and in its towns will once again use these words: “May the LORD bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain!” 24Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with the flocks. 25For I refresh the weary soul and satisfy everyone who is faint. 26At this I woke up and looked around, and my sleep had been sweet to me.

27The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow seed in the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the seed of people and the seed of animals. 28Just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to overthrow, to destroy and to bring harm, so I will keep watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD. 29In those days people will no longer say, “The parents ate sour grapes, but it is the children whose teeth are set on edge.” 30Instead, each will die for their own guilt; whoever eats the sour grapes, it is their own teeth that will be set on edge.

A new covenant

31The days are coming, declares the LORD, and then I will make a covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah: a new covenant. 32It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors on the day I took their hand to lead them out from the land of Egypt. They broke my covenant, though I was their husband, declares the LORD. 33Rather, this will be the covenant that I make with the house of Israel when those days are past, declares the LORD: I will set my instruction deep inside them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people. 34No longer will each one teach their neighbor, or each one their brother or sister, saying, “Know the LORD,” because all of them will know me, from the least to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their guilt, and I will remember their sin no more.

35The LORD says this, the LORD who gives the sun to light the day and the moon and stars in their fixed order to light the night, who stirs up the sea until its waves roar; the LORD of Armies is his name: 36Only if this fixed order ever failed before me, declares the LORD, would the descendants of Israel ever cease to be a nation before me.

37The LORD says this: Only if someone could measure the heavens above and search out the foundations of the earth below would I reject all the descendants of Israel because of all they have done, declares the LORD.

38The days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate. 39The measuring line will stretch out farther, straight to the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah. 40The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields out to the Kidron Valley, as far as the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. Never again will it be uprooted or overthrown.
fields.summary: God’s love for Israel is everlasting, and Rachel’s weeping for her children will end. God will make a new covenant, writing the law on their hearts.

fields.title: Jeremiah 32
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah buys his cousin’s field

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah’s reign over Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar’s reign. 2The army of the king of Babylon was then laying siege to Jerusalem, and the prophet Jeremiah was being held in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah, 3for Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him there. He had said, “Why do you prophesy as you do? You say, ‘The LORD says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it. 4Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Chaldeans. He will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon; he will speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes. 5He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and Zedekiah will stay there until I deal with him, declares the LORD. Even if you fight the Chaldeans, you will have no success.’”

6Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me: 7“Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is going to come to you and say, ‘Buy my field at Anathoth, for as the family redeemer you have the right to buy it.’” 8Then my cousin Hanamel visited me in the courtyard of the guard, just as the LORD had said. He told me, “Please buy my field at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin. The right of inheritance is yours, and so is the right of redemption; buy it for yourself.” I knew then that this was the word of the LORD. 9So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out the price for him: about 7 ounces of silver. 10I signed the deed and sealed it, had it witnessed, and weighed the silver on scales. 11Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy. 12I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, while my cousin Hanamel looked on, along with the witnesses who had signed the deed and all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard. 13In their presence I gave Baruch these instructions: 14“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Take these documents, this deed of purchase, both the sealed copy and the open one, and put them in a clay jar so that they will last for a long time.

15For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: People will once more buy houses, fields and vineyards in this land.”

Jeremiah prays

16Once I had given Baruch son of Neriah the deed of purchase, I prayed to the LORD: 17“Oh, Lord GOD! You are the one who made the heavens and the earth with your great strength, with your arm stretched out. There is nothing too hard for you. 18You show loyal love to thousands, yet you pay back the guilt of parents into the laps of their children after them. You are the great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of Armies, 19great in purpose and mighty in action. Your eyes are open to all the ways of humankind, to give each person what their ways deserve and what the fruit of their deeds has earned. 20You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt and have done so to this day, both in Israel and among all humankind. You have made a name for yourself that is known to this day. 21With signs and wonders you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt, by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror. 22You gave them this land that you had sworn to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey. 23They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey your voice or live by your instruction. They did nothing of all you had commanded them to do, and so you have made all this disaster fall on them. 24Look, the siege ramps have reached the city to take it. Because of sword, famine and plague, the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans who are attacking it. What you said has come about, and you can see it. 25Yet you, Lord GOD, have told me, ‘Buy the field with silver and have the sale witnessed,’ though the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans!” 26Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 27“Look, I am the LORD, the God of all humanity. Is there anything too hard for me? 28Therefore the LORD says this: I am about to hand this city over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it. 29The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will enter it and set it ablaze. They will burn it, and the houses too, where people burned incense to Baal on the roofs and poured drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger. 30From their youth the Israelites and the people of Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight. The Israelites have done nothing but provoke me with what their hands have made, declares the LORD. 31This city has stirred up my anger and my fury from the day it was built until now, so that I must remove it from my sight, 32because of all the evil the Israelites and the people of Judah have done to provoke me: they themselves, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets, the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem. 33They have turned their backs to me, not their faces. I taught them again and again, but they did not listen or accept correction. 34They placed their detestable idols in the house that bears my name and so defiled it. 35They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire for Molech, a thing I never commanded them and that never entered my mind, that they should do this detestable thing and so lead Judah into sin.

An everlasting covenant

36But now the LORD, the God of Israel, says this about this city, of which you are saying, ‘It is being handed over to the king of Babylon by sword, famine and plague’: 37I am going to gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in my anger, my rage and my great fury. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety. 38They will be my people, and I will be their God. 39I will give them one heart and one way, so they will fear me for all time. It will be for their good, and for the good of their children who come after them. 40I will make with them a covenant that is everlasting: I will not turn back from them, but will keep on doing them good. I will put the fear of me in their hearts so that they never turn aside from me. 41I will delight in doing them good. With all my heart and all my soul I will plant them faithfully in this land.

42For the LORD says this: As I have brought on this people all this great disaster, so I will bring on them all the good I promise them. 43Fields will be bought in this land of which you are saying, ‘It is a desolate waste, with no people or animals; it has been handed over to the Chaldeans.’ 44People will buy fields with silver, sign deeds, seal them and have them witnessed, in Benjamin’s territory and the places around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah and the towns of the hill country, and in the towns of the western foothills and of the Negev, for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.”
fields.summary: During the siege Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth as a sign that houses and fields will again be bought in the land. God promises an everlasting covenant.

fields.title: Jeremiah 33
fields.body_html:
