Healing for the city

1The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still held in the courtyard of the guard: 2“The LORD says this, the LORD who made it, the LORD who formed it and set it firm; the LORD is his name: 3Call out to me, and I will answer you. I will make known to you great things, things beyond your reach, which you have not known.

4For the LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, which have been torn down to hold back the siege ramps and the sword: 5They come to fight against the Chaldeans, but only to fill these houses with the dead bodies of the people I have struck down in my anger and my rage; for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil. 6But look, I will bring this city recovery and a cure. I will heal its people and show them peace and stability in abundance. 7I will restore the fortunes of Judah and of Israel, and I will rebuild them as they were at the beginning. 8I will cleanse them from all the guilt of their sin against me, and I will forgive all their guilt, every way they have sinned against me and rebelled against me. 9This city will be for me a name of joy, praise and glory before all the nations of the earth. They will hear of all the good I do for its people, and they will be in awe and tremble because of all the good and all the peace I bring about for it.

10The LORD says this: Once more there will be heard in this place, which you call a ruin with neither people nor animals, in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that lie deserted, without people, without anyone living there, without animals, 11the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, and the voices of those who say, ‘Give the LORD of Armies thanks, for the LORD is good; his loyal love lasts forever,’ as they bring offerings of thanks to the house of the LORD. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as they were at the beginning, says the LORD.

12The LORD of Armies says this: In this place that lies in ruins, without people or animals, and in all its towns, there will once again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks. 13In the towns of the hill country, of the western foothills and of the Negev, in Benjamin’s territory, in the places surrounding Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says the LORD.

The righteous Branch

14The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will carry out the good promise I made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
15In those days and at that time
I will make a righteous Branch spring up for David,
and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
16In those days Judah will be saved,
and Jerusalem will live in safety.
And this is the name people will give her: ‘The LORD Is Our Righteousness.’

17For the LORD says this: David will always have a man of his line to sit on the throne of the house of Israel. 18Nor will the priests, the Levites, ever be without a man who serves in my presence, offering burnt offerings, burning grain offerings and making sacrifices for all time.”

The covenant with day and night

19The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 20“The LORD says this: If you could break my covenant with day and my covenant with night, and stop day and night from coming at their set times, 21then my covenant with my servant David could also be broken, and he would have no son to reign on his throne; and so could my covenant with the Levites, the priests who serve me. 22As the stars of the sky cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of my servant David and the Levites who serve me.”

23The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 24“Have you not seen what these people are saying: ‘The LORD chose two families, and now he has rejected them’? So they look down on my people, as if they were no longer a nation in their eyes.

25The LORD says this: If I had not made my covenant with day and night, if I had not set in place the fixed laws of heaven and earth, 26then I would also reject Jacob’s descendants and those of my servant David, and not take rulers from David’s line to govern the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Indeed, I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.”
fields.summary: God promises to heal and restore Jerusalem and to raise up a righteous Branch for David. God’s covenant with David and the Levites is as sure as day and night.

fields.title: Jeremiah 34
fields.body_html:
A message for King Zedekiah

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon was making war on Jerusalem and all its towns, with his whole army and all the kingdoms and peoples of the earth that were under his rule: 2“The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, ‘The LORD says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down. 3You yourself will not escape from him. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will look the king of Babylon in the eye, and he will speak to you face to face. And you will go to Babylon. 4But hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah. The LORD says this about you: You will not die by the sword. 5You will die in peace. As spices were burned in honor of your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you, so people will burn spices in your honor and mourn for you, crying, ‘Alas, my lord!’ I have given my word, declares the LORD.’”

6Jeremiah the prophet told Zedekiah king of Judah all these things in Jerusalem, 7while the king of Babylon’s army was attacking Jerusalem and the towns of Judah that were still holding out, Lachish and Azekah. These were the only fortified towns of Judah that remained.

Freed slaves taken back

8This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah and all the people in Jerusalem had made a covenant to announce freedom, 9so that everyone would set free their Hebrew slaves, both men and women, and no one would keep a fellow Judean as a slave. 10All the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant agreed to set free their male and female slaves and not keep them as slaves any longer. They obeyed and let them go. 11But afterward they changed their minds. They took back the men and women they had set free and forced them to be their slaves again.

12Then the word of the LORD came from the LORD to Jeremiah: 13“The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: I made a covenant with your ancestors when I led them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house where they were slaves. I said: 14‘At the close of every seven years, each of you must release any fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you as a slave. When that person has served you six years, you must send them away free.’ But your ancestors did not listen to me or pay attention. 15Just now you yourselves turned back and did what is right in my sight: each of you announced freedom for your neighbor, and you made a covenant in my presence in the house that bears my name. 16But then you turned around and profaned my name. Each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go where they wished, and you forced them to be your slaves again.

17Therefore the LORD says this: You have not obeyed me by announcing freedom, each of you for your fellow Hebrew and your neighbor. So now I am announcing freedom for you, declares the LORD: freedom to fall by the sword, the plague and the famine. I will make you a horror to every kingdom on earth. 18As for the people who broke my covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me, I will make them like the calf they cut in two and walked between its halves, 19that is, the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the court officers, the priests and all the people of the land who walked between the halves of the calf. 20I will hand them over to their enemies, to those who want them dead, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and for the wild animals. 21Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will hand over to their enemies, to those who want them dead, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you. 22I am about to give the order, declares the LORD. I will bring them back to this city, and they will attack it, take it and burn it down. I will turn the towns of Judah into a desolate waste where no one lives.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah that he will be taken to Babylon. The people free their Hebrew slaves and then take them back, and God condemns them.

fields.title: Jeremiah 35
fields.body_html:
The Rechabites keep their ancestor’s command

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: 2“Go to the family of the Rechabites and speak with them. Bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the side rooms, and give them wine to drink.” 3So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, with his brothers and all his sons, the whole family of the Rechabites. 4I brought them into the house of the LORD, to the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the officials’ room, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the doorkeeper. 5Then I set pitchers full of wine and cups before the men of the Rechabite family, and I said to them, “Drink some wine.” 6But they answered, “We do not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us, ‘You must never drink wine, neither you nor your descendants. 7You must not build a house, sow seed or plant a vineyard; you must not own any of them. Instead, you must stay in tents all your lives, so that you may live many days in the land where you are outsiders.’ 8We have obeyed our ancestor Jehonadab son of Rechab in everything he commanded us: we do not drink wine as long as we live, neither we nor our wives, our sons or our daughters, 9and not to build houses to live in. We have no vineyard, no field and no seed to sow. 10We have lived in tents and have obeyed and done everything our ancestor Jonadab commanded us. 11But when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, we said, ‘Come, let us go to Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Arameans.’ That is why we are living in Jerusalem.”

12Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah: 13“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Go and say to the people of Judah and to those who live in Jerusalem, ‘Will you not accept correction and listen to my words? declares the LORD. 14Jehonadab son of Rechab told his descendants not to drink wine, and his words have been kept: to this day they have not drunk it, because they obey their ancestor’s command. I, however, have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to me. 15I sent you all my servants the prophets again and again, saying, “Turn back, every one of you, from your evil way, and make your deeds good. Do not follow other gods to serve them, and you will live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors.” But you did not pay attention or listen to me. 16Yes, the descendants of Jehonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them, but this people has not listened to me.

17Therefore the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to bring on Judah and on all who live in Jerusalem all the disaster I have announced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.’” 18Then Jeremiah said to the family of the Rechabites, “The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jehonadab, kept all his commands and done all that he commanded you,

19therefore the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Jonadab son of Rechab will never be without a descendant to stand before me for all time.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah tests the Rechabites with wine, and they refuse because of their ancestor’s command. Their faithfulness is set against Judah’s disobedience.

fields.title: Jeremiah 36
fields.body_html:
Baruch writes and reads the scroll

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: 2“Take a scroll and write on it every word that I have spoken to you about Israel, about Judah and about all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until today. 3It may be that when the house of Judah hears about all the disaster I intend to bring on them, every one of them will turn back from their evil way, and I will forgive their guilt and their sin.”

4So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote down on a scroll everything the LORD had spoken to him. 5Then Jeremiah gave Baruch these instructions: “I am barred; I cannot go into the house of the LORD. 6So you must go, and on a fast day read the words of the LORD from the scroll you wrote at my dictation, in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD. Read them also in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come in from their towns. 7It may be that their plea for mercy will come before the LORD, and every one of them will turn back from their evil way. For the anger and fury that the LORD has declared against this people are great.” 8Baruch son of Neriah did everything the prophet Jeremiah had commanded him: he read the words of the LORD from the scroll in the house of the LORD.

9In the ninth month of the fifth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a fast was proclaimed before the LORD for all the people in Jerusalem and for all the people who came into Jerusalem from the towns of Judah. 10Then Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the scroll in the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people. He read from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD. 11When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD read from the scroll, 12he went down to the king’s palace, to the secretary’s chamber. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the other officials. 13Micaiah reported to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people. 14Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch to say, “Bring the scroll you read to the people, and come.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and went to them. 15They said to him, “Please sit down and read it to us.” So Baruch read it to them. 16When they heard all the words, they turned to one another in alarm and said to Baruch, “We must certainly report all these words to the king.” 17Then they asked Baruch, “Tell us, please, how did you come to write all these words? Was it at his dictation?” 18Baruch answered them, “He spoke all these words aloud to me, and I wrote them down in ink on the scroll.”

The king burns the scroll

19Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Do not let anyone know where you are.” 20They went in to the king in the courtyard, having left the scroll for safekeeping in the chamber of Elishama the secretary, and they reported all the words to the king. 21The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he brought it from the chamber of Elishama the secretary. Jehudi read it to the king and to all the officials who stood in attendance on him. 22It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter house, with a fire burning in the brazier in front of him. 23Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them away with a scribe’s knife and throw them on the fire in the brazier, until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire. 24Yet neither the king nor any of his officials who heard all these words was afraid, and they did not tear their clothes. 25Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah even pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, but he refused to listen to them. 26Instead, the king ordered Jerahmeel, the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and the prophet Jeremiah. But the LORD hid them.

The scroll is written again

27The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll, and with it the words Baruch had written as Jeremiah dictated: 28“Take another scroll and write on it again all the words that were on the first scroll, the one that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned. 29And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you are to say, ‘The LORD says this: You burned this scroll and said, “Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon is sure to come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals from it?”‘

30Therefore the LORD says this about Jehoiakim king of Judah: No one of his line will sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be thrown out to the heat of the day and the frost of the night. 31I will punish him and his descendants and his officials for their guilt. I will bring on them, on those who live in Jerusalem and on the people of Judah all the disaster I have pronounced against them, because they did not listen.”

32Then Jeremiah took another scroll and handed it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it every word of the scroll that King Jehoiakim of Judah had burned in the fire, and many other words like them were added.
fields.summary: Baruch writes Jeremiah’s words on a scroll and reads it in the temple. King Jehoiakim burns it piece by piece, and Jeremiah dictates it again.

fields.title: Jeremiah 37
fields.body_html:
Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to pray

1Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had made him king in the land of Judah. 2But neither he nor his officials nor the people of the land paid attention to the words the LORD spoke through the prophet Jeremiah. 3King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to the prophet Jeremiah with this request: “Please pray to the LORD our God for us.” 4At that time Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people; he had not yet been put in prison. 5Pharaoh’s army had marched out of Egypt. The Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the news about them and withdrew from the city.

6Then the word of the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah: 7“The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to seek my answer: ‘Pharaoh’s army, which has set out to help you, is going back to its own land, to Egypt. 8Then the Chaldeans will come back and attack this city. They will capture it and set it on fire.

9The LORD says this: Do not fool yourselves by thinking, “The Chaldeans are sure to leave us for good.” They will not leave. 10Even if you were to defeat the entire Chaldean army that is fighting against you, and only badly wounded men were left among them, each lying in his tent, they would still get up and burn this city down.’” 11When the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because Pharaoh’s army was approaching,

Jeremiah is arrested

12Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to receive his share of property there among the people. 13When he reached the Benjamin Gate, a captain of the guard named Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, was there. He arrested the prophet Jeremiah and said, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!” 14“That is a lie!” Jeremiah said. “I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” Irijah refused to listen. He arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials. 15The officials were furious with Jeremiah. They beat him and locked him up in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had turned into a prison. 16So Jeremiah was put in the cistern house, in its vaulted cells, and he stayed there for a long time.

Zedekiah questions Jeremiah in secret

17Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he questioned him in private. “Is there any word from the LORD?” the king asked. “There is,” Jeremiah replied. “You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”

18Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What wrong have I done to you or your officials or this people, that you have put me in prison? 19Where are your prophets now, who prophesied to you that the king of Babylon would not come against you or against this land? 20Now please listen, my lord the king. Please accept my plea: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there.” 21So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the court of the guard. Each day he was given a loaf of bread from the street of the bakers, until there was no bread left in the city. And Jeremiah stayed in the court of the guard.
fields.summary: Jeremiah is arrested and imprisoned on a charge of deserting to the Babylonians. Zedekiah consults him secretly and keeps him in the courtyard of the guard.

fields.title: Jeremiah 38
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah is lowered into a cistern

1Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people:

2“The LORD says this: ‘Those who stay in this city will die by sword, famine and plague. But those who go out to the Chaldeans will live; they will come away with their lives as their only plunder, and they will live.’

3The LORD says this: ‘This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon’s army, and he will capture it.’” 4Then the officials said to the king, “This man must be put to death. By saying such things he is weakening the resolve of the soldiers who are left in this city, and of all the people as well. This man is not seeking the good of this people, but their harm.” 5King Zedekiah said, “Very well, he is in your hands. The king can do nothing to oppose you.” 6So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king’s son, in the courtyard of the guard. They let him down with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.

7Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court officer in the king’s palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. At the time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate. 8So Ebed-melech went out of the palace and spoke to the king: 9“My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, and he will die there of hunger, for there is no bread left in the city.” 10Then the king gave Ebed-melech the Cushite this order: “Take thirty men with you from here, and pull Jeremiah the prophet up from the cistern before he dies.” 11So Ebed-melech went into the palace with the men, to a room beneath the storehouse. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and let them down on ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern. 12Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your armpits, between you and the ropes.” Jeremiah did so. 13Then they drew Jeremiah up by the ropes and brought him out of the cistern, and Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

Zedekiah questions Jeremiah again

14King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to him at the third entrance of the house of the LORD. The king said to Jeremiah, “I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me.” 15Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “If I tell you, will you not certainly have me put to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.” 16But King Zedekiah swore an oath to Jeremiah in secret: “As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us this life, I will not put you to death, and I will not hand you over to these men who want to kill you.”

17Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “The LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: ‘If you will surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned down. You and your family will live. 18But if you do not surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it down. And you yourself will not escape from them.’”

19King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans. They may hand me over to them, and they will treat me cruelly.”

20Jeremiah said, “They will not hand you over. Please obey the LORD’s voice in what I am telling you. Then it will go well with you, and your life will be spared. 21But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:
22Look, all the women who are left in the palace of the king of Judah are being led out to the commanders of the king of Babylon,
and they are saying, ‘Your trusted friends
have misled you and overpowered you;
now your feet are sunk in the mud,
they have turned their backs on you.’
23All your wives and your children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape from them. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and you will be the cause of this city being burned down.”

24Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone know about this conversation, and you will not die. 25If the officials hear that I have talked with you, and they come and say to you, ‘Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide anything from us, and we will not put you to death,’ 26then say to them, ‘I was presenting my plea to the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.’”

27All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he answered them with the very words the king had told him to say. So they stopped questioning him, for no one had overheard the conversation.

28So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem fell. This is what happened when Jerusalem was captured:
fields.summary: The officials throw Jeremiah into a muddy cistern, and Ebed-melech the Cushite rescues him. Zedekiah again consults Jeremiah, who urges him to surrender.

fields.title: Jeremiah 39
fields.body_html:
Babylon captures Jerusalem

1In the tenth month of the ninth year of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon advanced on Jerusalem with his whole army, and they laid siege to it.

2In the fourth month of Zedekiah’s eleventh year, on the ninth day of the month, the city wall was breached. 3Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came in and took their seats in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebu, Sarsekim the chief of the court officials, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon. 4When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers caught sight of them, they fled. They went out of the city at night, taking the road by the king’s garden, through the gate between the two walls, and the king went off toward the Arabah. 5But the Chaldean army chased them and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and took him up to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and there the king passed sentence on him. 6At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons while he watched; the king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah. 7Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him in bronze fetters to take him to Babylon. 8The Chaldeans burned down the king’s palace and the houses of the people, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem. 9Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile to Babylon the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people who remained. 10But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left in the land of Judah some of the poor people who owned nothing, and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields. 11Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, saying, 12“Take him and look after him. Do him no harm, but do for him whatever he asks of you.” 13So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the chief of the court officials, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag and all the king of Babylon’s chief officers sent word, 14and had Jeremiah brought from the court of the guard. They entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him home, and he stayed among the people.

A promise for Ebed-melech

15The word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah while he was confined in the court of the guard: 16“Go and tell Ebed-melech the Cushite, ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Look, I am about to carry out my words against this city, for disaster and not for good. On that day you will see them come true. 17But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD; you will not be handed over to the men you are afraid of. 18I will certainly rescue you; you will not fall by the sword. You will come away with your life as your plunder, because you have trusted in me, declares the LORD.’”
fields.summary: Babylon captures Jerusalem, Zedekiah is blinded and taken captive, and the city is burned. Jeremiah is released, and Ebed-melech is promised safety.

fields.title: Jeremiah 40
fields.body_html:
Jeremiah freed at Ramah

1This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had set him free at Ramah. Nebuzaradan had found him there bound in chains, among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile in Babylon. 2The captain of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, “The LORD your God announced this disaster against this place. 3Now the LORD has brought it about and has done just what he said, because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey his voice. That is why this has happened to you. 4But now, today I am setting you free from the chains on your wrists. If you would like to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if you would rather not come with me to Babylon, then stay. See, the whole land lies open before you. Go wherever you think it good and right to go.” 5Before Jeremiah had turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, “Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, the man the king of Babylon has set over the towns of Judah, and live with him among the people. Or go anywhere else you think right.” Then the captain of the guard gave him food for the journey and a gift, and let him go. 6So Jeremiah went to Mizpah, to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and lived there with him among the people left in the land.

Gedaliah at Mizpah

7All the commanders of the forces who were in the open country and their men learned that the king of Babylon had set Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had placed in his care men, women and children, those of the poorest people of the land who had not been taken into exile to Babylon, 8and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, together with their men. 9Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, gave them and their men his sworn word. “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans,” he said. “Settle in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and all will go well with you. 10As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you are to gather the wine, the summer fruit and the oil, store them in your jars, and live in the towns you have taken over.” 11Likewise, all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had allowed a remnant to stay in Judah, with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, set over them, 12and all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been scattered. They came back to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and brought in a very large harvest of wine and summer fruit.

13Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah 14and asked him, “Do you realize that Baalis, the Ammonite king, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to murder you?” Gedaliah son of Ahikam, however, would not believe them. 15Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah privately at Mizpah. “Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah,” he said, “and no one will know. Why should he take your life, so that all the Judeans gathered around you are scattered and the remnant of Judah perishes?” 16But Gedaliah son of Ahikam answered Johanan son of Kareah, “You must not do this! What you are saying about Ishmael is false.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah stays with Gedaliah, the new governor at Mizpah. Gedaliah is warned of a plot against him but does not believe it.

fields.title: Jeremiah 41
fields.body_html:
Ishmael kills Gedaliah

1In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was of royal descent and one of the king’s chief officers, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, bringing ten men with him. There at Mizpah they ate a meal together. 2Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword. So he killed the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land. 3Ishmael also struck down all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldean soldiers who happened to be there. 4On the day after Gedaliah’s murder, before anyone knew about it, 5eighty men arrived from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria. Their beards were shaved, their clothes torn and their bodies gashed, and they were carrying grain offerings and frankincense to bring to the house of the LORD. 6Ishmael son of Nethaniah left Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went along. When he met them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”

7But as soon as they were inside the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and his men slaughtered them and threw them into the cistern. 8But there were ten men among them who said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us! We have stores of wheat, barley, oil and honey hidden in the countryside.” So he held back and did not kill them along with their companions. 9The cistern where Ishmael threw the bodies of all the men he had struck down along with Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made for defense against Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with those he had killed. 10Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who were at Mizpah: the king’s daughters and all the others left at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had placed in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah carried them off as captives and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.

Johanan brings the captives back

11When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him heard of all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done, 12they took all their men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great pool in Gibeon. 13When all the people Ishmael had with him saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him, they were glad. 14All the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and went back over to Johanan son of Kareah. 15But Ishmael son of Nethaniah got away from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

16Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him took charge of all the rest of the people from Mizpah. Johanan had rescued them from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after the murder of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. They were fighting men, women, children and court officers, whom Johanan had brought back from Gibeon. 17They set out and stopped at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, on their way to Egypt, 18to escape the Chaldeans. They were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land.
fields.summary: Ishmael son of Nethaniah murders Gedaliah and many others. Johanan rescues the captives, and they plan to flee to Egypt.

fields.title: Jeremiah 42
fields.body_html:
The leaders ask for a word

1Then all the commanders of the forces came forward, including Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, with all the people from the least to the greatest. 2They said to the prophet Jeremiah, “Please hear our request, and pray to the LORD your God for us, for all this remnant. There were many of us, but only a few are left, as you can see for yourself. 3Let the LORD your God tell us where we should go and what we should do.” 4The prophet Jeremiah said to them, “I have heard you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you ask. Whatever the LORD answers, I will tell you; I will not keep back a single word from you.” 5They said to Jeremiah, “If we fail to do all that the LORD your God sends you to tell us, may the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us. 6Whether we find it good or bad, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you. When we obey the voice of the LORD our God, it will go well with us.”

Stay in the land; do not go to Egypt

7Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah. 8So he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him. He summoned all the people as well, from the least to the greatest. 9He said to them, “You sent me to the LORD, the God of Israel, to lay your plea before him, and he says this: 10If you will stay in this land, I will build you and not tear you down, and I will plant you and not uproot you, because I relent concerning the disaster I have brought on you. 11Do not fear the king of Babylon, though you are afraid of him now. Do not fear him, declares the LORD. I am with you, and I will save you and rescue you from his power. 12I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and let you return to your own land. 13But suppose you say, ‘We will not stay in this land,’ and so disobey the voice of the LORD your God, 14and say, ‘No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no ram’s horn sounding and never go hungry for bread. That is where we will live,’ 15then hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: If you are set on going to Egypt, and you go to settle there, 16then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close behind you into Egypt, and you will die there. 17All the people who are set on going to Egypt to settle there will die by sword, famine and plague. No one among them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing on them.

18For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Just as my anger and my fury were poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so my fury will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a name used in curses, a horror, a curse and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again. 19The LORD has told you, remnant of Judah, ‘Do not go to Egypt.’ Know for certain that I have warned you today. 20You have deceived yourselves, and it will cost you your lives. You yourselves sent me to the LORD your God and said, ‘Pray for us to the LORD our God. Tell us everything the LORD our God says, and we will do it.’ 21Today I have told you, yet you have not obeyed the LORD your God in anything he sent me to tell you. 22So now know for certain that you will die by sword, famine and plague in the place where you want to go and settle.”
fields.summary: The people ask Jeremiah to seek God’s guidance, and God tells them to stay in the land and not go to Egypt.

fields.title: Jeremiah 43
fields.body_html:
Into Egypt against the warning

1When Jeremiah finished speaking to all the people every word of the LORD their God, all the words the LORD their God had sent him to give them,

2then Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah, with all the arrogant men, answered Jeremiah, “What you say is a lie! The LORD our God did not send you to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to settle there.’ 3Baruch son of Neriah is the one stirring you up against us, so that we will be handed over to the Chaldeans, to be killed or carried off to Babylon.” 4So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces and all the people refused to obey the command the LORD gave them to remain in the land of Judah. 5But Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces led away the whole remnant of Judah, those who had come back from all the nations where they had been scattered in order to live in the land of Judah: 6the men, the women and the children, the king’s daughters, and everyone whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and also the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch son of Neriah. 7So they went into the land of Egypt, since they did not obey the LORD, and came as far as Tahpanhes.

Stones hidden at Tahpanhes

8The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes: 9“Take some large stones in your hands and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance of Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, while the men of Judah watch. 10Then tell them, ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to send for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and bring him here. I will set his throne over these stones that I have buried, and he will spread his royal canopy over them. 11He will come and strike the land of Egypt: whoever is marked out for death, to death; whoever is marked out for captivity, to captivity; and whoever is marked out for the sword, to the sword. 12I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry them off as captives. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there unharmed. 13He will smash the sacred pillars of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and set the temples of the gods of Egypt on fire.’”
fields.summary: The leaders accuse Jeremiah of lying and take the people, Jeremiah and Baruch to Egypt. In Tahpanhes Jeremiah foretells that Nebuchadnezzar will conquer Egypt.

fields.title: Jeremiah 44
fields.body_html:
Judeans in Egypt warned

1This message came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt, at Migdol, Tahpanhes and Memphis, and in the land of Pathros:

2“The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: You have seen for yourselves all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they lie in ruins, and no one lives in them, 3because of the evil they did to provoke me to anger. They went and burned incense and served other gods that neither they nor you nor your ancestors had ever known. 4Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets to say, ‘Please do not do this detestable thing that I hate!’ 5But they did not listen or pay attention. They would not turn from their evil and stop burning incense to other gods. 6So my fury and my anger poured out and blazed in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they became the ruined wasteland they are today.

7So now the LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves? You are cutting off man and woman, child and infant, from among Judah, and leaving yourselves no remnant, 8by provoking me to anger with what your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in Egypt, the land you have come to live in? It will only cut you off and make you a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth. 9Have you forgotten the wicked deeds of your ancestors, of the kings of Judah and their wives, your own wicked deeds and those of your wives, which were done in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? 10To this day they have not been humbled, and they have shown no fear. They have not lived by my instruction and my statutes, which I set before you and your ancestors.

11Therefore the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am setting my face against you to bring harm, to cut off all Judah. 12I will take away the remnant of Judah who were determined to go to the land of Egypt to live there, and they will all perish in the land of Egypt. They will fall by the sword or perish by famine; least and greatest alike will die by sword and famine. They will become a name used in curses, a horror, a curse and a disgrace. 13Those who live in the land of Egypt I will punish as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine and plague. 14Of the remnant of Judah who have come to live in the land of Egypt, none will escape or survive to go back to the land of Judah, though they long to return and live there. None will return except a few fugitives.”

Incense for the queen of heaven

15Then a great assembly answered Jeremiah: all the men who were aware that their wives burned incense to other gods, all the women standing by, and all the people living in Pathros in the land of Egypt. They said: 16“That message you spoke to us in the name of the LORD: we are not going to listen to you. 17Instead, we will do everything we have promised: we will burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials did in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Back then we had plenty of food, we were well off, and we saw no disaster. 18But from the time we gave up burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring drink offerings out to her, we have been in need of everything and have been wiped out by sword and famine.” 19“And when we were burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring drink offerings out to her, did we make cakes bearing her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands’ consent?”

20Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people, the men and the women, all the people who had given him this answer. He said: 21“The incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, you and your ancestors, your kings and your officials, and the people of the land: has the LORD not remembered it, and has it not come into his mind? 22The LORD could no longer bear your evil deeds and the detestable things you did, so your land became a ruin, a horror and a curse, with no one living in it, as it is today. 23It is because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, and would not listen to the voice of the LORD or live by his instruction, his statutes and his decrees, that this disaster has come upon you, as it has today.”

24Then Jeremiah said to all the people and all the women, “Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

25The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: You and your wives have said it with your mouths and carried it out with your hands: ‘We will certainly keep the vows we made, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.’ Go ahead, then: keep your vows! Carry out your vows!

26Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who live in the land of Egypt: I swear by my great name, says the LORD, that in all the land of Egypt my name will never again be invoked by anyone from Judah who says, ‘As surely as the Lord GOD lives.’ 27I am keeping watch over them for harm and not for good. All the people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are wiped out. 28Those who escape the sword and return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah will be very few. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to live there will know whose word comes true, mine or theirs. 29This will be the sign to you, declares the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words of harm against you will certainly come true:

30The LORD says this: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, who wanted to kill him.”
fields.summary: Jeremiah rebukes the Judeans in Egypt for burning incense to the queen of heaven, and they refuse to listen.

fields.title: Jeremiah 45
fields.body_html:
A promise to Baruch

1This is the word that the prophet Jeremiah spoke to Baruch son of Neriah in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, when Baruch wrote these words in a scroll at Jeremiah’s dictation:

2“The LORD, the God of Israel, says this to you, Baruch: 3You have said, ‘Woe is me! The LORD has heaped sorrow on top of my pain. I am weary from my groaning, and I can find no rest.’

4Say this to him: ‘The LORD says this: What I have built I am about to tear down, and what I have planted I am about to uproot, the whole land. 5As for you, are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am about to bring disaster on all humankind, declares the LORD, but I will let you come away with your life as your plunder wherever you go.’”
fields.summary: God tells Baruch that he will escape with his life wherever he goes.

fields.title: Jeremiah 46
fields.body_html:
Egypt’s army at Carchemish

1This message from the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah about the nations: 2About Egypt. About the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, camped by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
3Make ready the small shield and the large,
and advance into battle!
4Harness the horses! Mount the warhorses!
Take your positions with helmets on!
Sharpen the spears,
put on your coats of mail!
5Why do I see them panic-stricken, falling back?
Their warriors are battered down;
they run headlong and do not look back.
Terror on every side! declares the LORD.
6The swift cannot run away,
the warrior cannot escape.
In the north, beside the Euphrates River,
they have stumbled and fallen.
7Who is this rising like the Nile,
like rivers with surging waters?
8Egypt rises like the Nile,
like rivers with surging waters.
Egypt said, “I will rise and cover the earth;
I will destroy cities and the people who live in them.”
9Charge, you horses! Race wildly, you chariots!
Let the warriors march out,
Cush and Put, who carry the shield,
and the Ludites, skilled archers.
10But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies, a day of vengeance, when he takes vengeance on his enemies.
The sword will devour until it is full,
until it has drunk its fill of their blood.
For the Lord GOD of Armies holds a sacrifice in the north country by the Euphrates River.
11Go up to Gilead and get balm,
Virgin Daughter Egypt!
You have tried remedy after remedy, but in vain;
there is no healing for you.
12The nations have heard of your disgrace;
the earth is full of your cries.
One warrior has stumbled over another,
and both have fallen together.

Egypt will be struck

13The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon coming to attack the land of Egypt:
14Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol,
proclaim it in Memphis and in Tahpanhes.
Say, “Take your position and make ready,
for the sword is devouring all around you.”
15Why is your mighty one swept away?
He could not stand,
for the LORD drove him down.
16He made many stumble;
they fell over one another. And they said, “Up! Let us go back to our own people and to the land where we were born,
away from the oppressor’s sword!”
17There they cried out,
“Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise;
he has let his moment pass.”
18As I live, declares the King,
the LORD of Armies is his name,
one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains,
like Carmel by the sea.
19Pack your bags for exile,
you people of Daughter Egypt!
For Memphis will become a wasteland,
a ruin where no one lives.

20Egypt is a lovely young heifer,
but a gadfly from the north is coming, coming on!
21Even the hired soldiers in her ranks are like fattened calves;
they too have turned and fled together, they did not stand their ground;
for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
22She makes a sound like a snake slithering away,
as her enemies march in force
and come at her with axes,
like woodcutters felling trees.
23They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD,
dense as it is,
for they are more than locusts;
they cannot be counted.
24Daughter Egypt is put to shame,
handed over to the people of the north.
25The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am about to punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and all who trust in him. 26I will hand them over to those who want to kill them, to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and his officials. But afterward Egypt will be lived in again as in former days, declares the LORD.

Comfort for Jacob

27But you, Jacob my servant, do not be afraid; do not be dismayed, Israel.
For I will save you from a far country, and your descendants from the land where they are captives.
Jacob will come home and have quiet and rest, and no one will make him afraid.

28You, Jacob my servant, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, because I am with you.
I will bring to an end all the nations among whom I drove you, but you I will not bring to an end.
I will discipline you, but justly,
and I will not let you go unpunished.
fields.summary: Jeremiah announces that Babylon will defeat Egypt at Carchemish and invade the land.

fields.title: Jeremiah 47
fields.body_html:
The Philistines

1This message from the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah about the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:

2The LORD says this: See, waters are rising in the north;
they will become a torrent in flood
and sweep over the land and everything in it,
the city and all who live there.
People will cry out,
and everyone who lives in the land will wail.
3At the sound of his stallions’ hooves pounding,
at the clatter of his chariots and the rumble of their wheels,
fathers do not turn back for their children;
their hands hang limp,
4because the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines
and to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every ally they have left.
For the LORD is destroying the Philistines,
what is left of the coastland of Caphtor.
5Gaza has shaved its head in mourning;
Ashkelon is silenced, the remnant of their valley.
How long will you gash yourself?

6Ah, sword of the LORD,
how long before you are quiet?
Go back into your sheath;
rest and be still.
7But how can you be quiet
when the LORD has given you orders?
Against Ashkelon and the seacoast, there he has sent you.
fields.summary: Jeremiah announces judgment on the Philistines.

fields.title: Jeremiah 48
fields.body_html:
Moab’s ruin

1Concerning Moab. The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Woe to Nebo, for it lies in ruins!
Kiriathaim is disgraced and captured;
the stronghold is disgraced and shattered.
2Moab’s renown is gone.
In Heshbon they have plotted disaster against her:
“Come, let us wipe her out as a nation.”
You too, Madmen, will be silenced;
the sword will pursue you.
3Listen! A cry from Horonaim:
ruin and great destruction!
4Moab is shattered;
its little ones cry out for all to hear.
5Up the climb to Luhith
they go weeping, weeping all the way;
on the way down to Horonaim
they have heard the anguished cry of disaster.
6Run! Save your lives!
Be like a bare shrub in the wilderness!
7Because you trusted in your achievements and your treasures,
you too will be taken.
Chemosh will go off into exile,
together with his priests and his officials.
8The destroyer will come upon every town; not one town will escape.
The valley will be ruined and the plateau laid waste,
just as the LORD has said.
9Give Moab wings,
for she must fly away;
her towns will become a wasteland,
with no one left living there.
10Cursed is anyone who does the work of the LORD carelessly,
and cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from shedding blood.
11Moab has lived at ease since his youth, resting undisturbed on his dregs,
never poured out from jar to jar,
never carried off into exile.
So his flavor has stayed in him,
and his aroma is unchanged.

12So the days are coming, declares the LORD,
when I will send him men who tip out jars, and they will tip him out;
they will empty his vessels
and smash their jars to pieces.
13Moab will be shamed by Chemosh,
as the house of Israel was shamed
by Bethel, the god they relied on.
14How can you claim,
“We are warriors,
strong men fit for battle”?
15Moab is ruined, and the enemy has gone up into her towns;
the finest of her young men have gone down to be slaughtered,
declares the King,
whose name is the LORD of Armies.
16Moab’s downfall is close at hand;
its disaster is rushing on.
17Grieve for him, all you his neighbors,
all who know his fame;
say, “How the mighty scepter is broken,
the glorious staff!”
18Come down from your glory and sit on the parched ground,
you who live in Daughter Dibon,
for Moab’s destroyer has come up against you;
he has torn down your fortresses.
19Stand by the road and keep watch, you who live in Aroer!
Ask the man who is running and the woman who is escaping;
ask them, “What has happened?”
20Moab is disgraced, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out!
Announce it by the Arnon:
Moab is ruined!
21Judgment has come on the land of the plateau: on Holon, Jahaz and Mephaath, 22on Dibon, Nebo and Beth-diblathaim, 23on Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul and Beth-meon, 24on Kerioth and Bozrah, and on all the towns of the land of Moab, far and near.
25Moab’s horn is hacked off,
and its arm is broken,
declares the LORD.
26Make him drunk,
for he has exalted himself against the LORD.
Moab will wallow in his own vomit,
and he too will become something to laugh at.
27Was not Israel a joke to you?
Was he caught among thieves,
that every time you spoke of him you shook your head in scorn?
28Abandon the towns and live among the rocks,
you people of Moab!
Be like a dove that makes its nest
in the cliffs beside the mouth of a gorge.
29We have heard of Moab’s pride, proud beyond measure:
its lofty looks, its pride, its haughty airs, its heart held high.
30I know its overbearing fury, declares the LORD; it is hollow.
Its big talk comes to nothing, and nothing they do turns out right.
31So I wail over Moab;
for all Moab I cry out;
for the men of Kir-heres there is moaning.
32More than Jazer weeps, I weep for you, vine of Sibmah.
Your runners crossed the sea
and reached as far as the sea of Jazer.
On your summer fruit and your grape harvest the destroyer has fallen.
33Gladness and delight are gathered up and gone from the garden land, from the land of Moab.
I have stopped the wine from flowing from the presses;
no one treads the grapes with the harvest shout.
The shouting is no shout of joy.
34The cry of Heshbon is heard in Elealeh; they raise their voices as far as Jahaz,
from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah.
Even the waters of Nimrim will turn to waste ground.
35I will put an end in Moab, declares the LORD,
to anyone who goes up to offer sacrifice at the high place
and burns incense to their gods.
36So my heart moans for Moab like a flute;
my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-heres.
So the riches they had amassed are lost.
37Every head is bald, every beard clipped short;
there are gashes on every hand, and sackcloth around the waist.
38On all the roofs of Moab and in its open squares there is nothing but mourning,
for I have smashed Moab like a jar that no one wants, declares the LORD.
39How shattered it is! How they wail!
How Moab has turned its back in shame!
Moab will become something to laugh at and a thing of horror to all its neighbors.

An eagle over Moab

40For the LORD says this:
Look! Like an eagle he swoops down
and spreads his wings over Moab.
41Kerioth is taken,
the strongholds are seized.
On that day the warriors of Moab will have hearts
like the heart of a woman in labor.
42Moab will be destroyed and no longer be a people,
because he exalted himself against the LORD.
43Fear and the pit and the trap
are upon you who live in Moab, declares the LORD.
44Anyone who runs from the fear will drop into the pit,
and anyone who climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the trap.
For I will bring on her, on Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
45In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand, their strength spent,
for fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the midst of Sihon.
It burned up the forehead of Moab,
the skulls of the people of tumult.
46Woe to you, Moab!
The people of Chemosh are destroyed.
Your sons have been taken away as captives,
and your daughters carried off into captivity.
47Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in days to come, declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.
fields.summary: Jeremiah announces the destruction of Moab and its pride, with a promise of restoration in days to come.

fields.title: Jeremiah 49
fields.body_html:
Ammon

1Concerning the Ammonites. The LORD says this:
Has Israel no children?
Has it no heir?
Then why has Milcom taken over Gad,
and why do his people live in its towns?
2So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make the battle cry ring out against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a mound of ruins,
and its villages will go up in flames.
Then Israel will drive out those who drove it out, says the LORD.
3Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry out, you villages of Rabbah!
Put on sackcloth
and mourn;
run back and forth inside the stone walls!
For Milcom will go into exile,
and his priests and officials with him.
4Why do you boast of your valleys,
your valley so rich,
you faithless daughter?
You trust in your treasures
and say, “Who would come against me?”
5I am about to bring terror on you from all who surround you, declares the Lord GOD of Armies.
You will be driven away, each of you running headlong,
and no one will gather those who flee.
6Yet afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares the LORD.

Edom

7Concerning Edom. The LORD of Armies says this:
Is there no wisdom left in Teman?
Have the wise run out of counsel?
Has their wisdom turned sour?
8Run! Turn and flee! Hide deep in the ground,
you who live in Dedan!
For I am bringing disaster on Esau, the time when I punish him.
9If grape pickers came to you,
would they not leave a few grapes behind?
If thieves came at night, they would ruin only as much as they wanted.
10But I have stripped Esau bare; I have laid open his hiding places,
and he cannot conceal himself.
His children, his relatives and his neighbors are destroyed, and he is gone.
11Leave your orphans behind; I will keep them alive.
Let your widows trust in me.

12For the LORD says this: If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it,
do you really think you will go unpunished?
You will not go unpunished;
you must drink it.
13For I swear by myself, declares the LORD,
that Bozrah will become a horror, a disgrace, a wasteland and a curse,
and all its towns will be ruins forever.
14I have heard news from the LORD;
a messenger has been sent among the nations:
“Gather together and attack her!
Rise up for battle!”
15For see, I will make you small among the nations,
despised by all people.
16The terror you strike into others and the pride of your heart have deceived you,
you who live in the clefts of the rock,
who hold the heights of the hill.
Though you build your nest as high as the eagle’s,
I will bring you down from there, declares the LORD.
17Edom will become a horror;
everyone who passes by
will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all its wounds.
18As when Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them were overthrown, says the LORD,
no one will live there;
no human being will settle in it.
19Look, an enemy will come up like a lion from the thick brush along the Jordan
against the pastures that never run dry.
In an instant I will chase Edom from its land,
and I will set over it the one I choose.
For who is like me? Who can call me to account?
What shepherd can stand against me?

20So hear the plan the LORD has made against Edom,
the purposes he has formed
against the people of Teman:
even the little ones of the flock will be dragged away;
he will make their pasture a desolate place because of them.
21At the sound of their fall
the earth shakes;
their cry is heard as far as the Red Sea.
22Look! Like an eagle he rises and swoops down
and spreads his wings over Bozrah.
On that day the warriors of Edom will have hearts
like the heart of a woman in labor.

Damascus, Kedar and Elam

23Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are dismayed,
for they have heard bad news, and their courage melts.
They are troubled like the sea,
which cannot be still.
24Damascus has lost her strength; she has turned to run, and panic has taken hold of her;
distress and pain grip her like a woman in labor.
25Why has the city of renown not been abandoned,
the town of my joy?
26So her young men will fall in her streets,
and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day,
declares the LORD of Armies.
27I will set fire to the wall of Damascus,
and it will burn up the fortresses of Ben-hadad.

28Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon defeated.
The LORD says this:
Rise up, march against Kedar,
and destroy the people of the east!
29Their tents and their flocks will be seized;
their tent curtains, all their goods and their camels will be carried off.
People will shout at them, “Terror on every side!”
30Run! Get far away! Hide deep in the ground, you who live in Hazor, declares the LORD.
For Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you;
he has worked out a scheme against you.
31Rise up and attack a nation at ease, living without a care, declares the LORD,
a nation with no gates and no bars, whose people live by themselves.
32Their camels will become plunder and their great herds spoil;
I will scatter to every wind those who clip the hair at their temples,
and I will bring disaster on them from every side, declares the LORD.
33Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a wasteland forever.
No one will live there;
no human being will settle in it.

34This message from the LORD came to the prophet Jeremiah about Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
35The LORD of Armies says this:
I am going to break the bow of Elam,
the mainstay of their strength.
36I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four ends of the heavens,
and I will scatter its people
to all these winds.
There will not be a nation
that Elam’s exiles do not reach.
37I will fill Elam with terror before their enemies, before those who want them dead. I will bring disaster on them, my fierce anger, declares the LORD.
I will send the sword after them
until I have finished them off.
38I will set up my throne in Elam
and destroy the king and officials there, declares the LORD.
39Yet in days to come I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.
fields.summary: Oracles of judgment are given against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Hazor and Elam.

fields.title: Jeremiah 50
fields.body_html:
Babylon’s fall

1This is the word that the LORD spoke about Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet:
2Announce it among the nations and proclaim it; raise a signal flag.
Proclaim it and hide nothing.
Say, “Babylon is taken; Bel is disgraced, Marduk is shattered.
Her images are disgraced, her idols are shattered.”
3For a nation from the north has come up against her.
It will turn her land into a waste, and no one will live in it.
People and animals alike have fled and are gone.
4In those days, at that time, declares the LORD,
the Israelites and the people of Judah will come together.
They will walk on, weeping as they go,
and they will seek the LORD their God.
5They will ask the way to Zion and set their faces toward it.
“Come!” they will say, and they will bind themselves to the LORD
in a covenant that lasts forever and will never be forgotten.

6My people have been lost sheep.
Their shepherds have led them astray
and let them roam on the mountains.
They have wandered from mountain to hill
and forgotten their resting place.
7All who came upon them devoured them,
and their enemies said, “We are not to blame,
for they sinned against the LORD, the pasture where they rightly belonged,
the LORD, in whom their ancestors hoped.”

8Flee from Babylon!
Get out of the land of the Chaldeans!
Be like the male goats that lead the flock.
9For I am about to stir up and bring against Babylon
a horde of great nations from the north country.
They will take up positions against her, and from there she will be taken.
Their arrows are like a warrior who leaves families childless;
they never come back empty.
10Chaldea will be looted;
all who loot her will have their fill, declares the LORD.
11Because you rejoice and gloat,
you who plunder my inheritance,
because you frisk like a heifer at the threshing
and neigh like stallions,
12your mother will be deeply ashamed;
she who gave you birth will be disgraced.
See, she will be the least of the nations,
a wilderness, a parched land, a desert.
13Because of the anger of the LORD no one will live in her;
she will be wholly desolate.
Everyone who passes by Babylon
will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all her wounds.
14Take up your positions around Babylon,
all you archers.
Shoot at her; do not hold back a single arrow,
for she has sinned against the LORD.
15Shout the battle cry against her on every side! She has surrendered;
her towers have fallen,
her walls are torn down.
This is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance on her;
do to her as she has done.
16Cut off from Babylon the one who sows
and the one who swings the sickle at harvest.
Before the oppressor’s sword
everyone will turn back to their own people;
everyone will flee to their own land.

Israel brought home

17Israel is a stray sheep chased off by lions.
First the king of Assyria devoured him;
now, last of all, he has had his bones gnawed
by Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.

18Therefore the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this:
I will bring punishment on the king of Babylon and on his land,
as I did to the king of Assyria.
19I will bring Israel back to his own pasture,
and he will graze on Carmel and in Bashan;
in the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead he will eat his fill.
20In those days, at that time, declares the LORD, the guilt of Israel will be searched for, but there will be none;
the sins of Judah, but they will not be found;
for I will forgive those I leave alive.
21Go up against the land of Merathaim,
and against those who live in Pekod.
Kill them and devote them to destruction to the very last, declares the LORD;
do everything I have commanded you.

22The noise of battle is in the land,
and great destruction!
23How the hammer of the whole earth
is cut down and shattered!
How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
24I laid a trap for you, Babylon, and it caught you
before you were aware of it.
You were found out and seized,
because you fought against the LORD.
25The LORD has opened his armory
and brought out the weapons of his wrath,
for the Lord GOD of Armies has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
26Come against her from the farthest places; break open her storehouses;
pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction.
Leave nothing of her.
27Kill all her young bulls;
let them go down to be slaughtered.
Woe to them,
for their day has arrived, the time for them to be punished.

28Listen! Fugitives and refugees are coming from the land of Babylon
to tell in Zion of the vengeance of the LORD our God,
vengeance for his temple.
29Call up archers against Babylon, all who draw the bow. Camp all around her; let no one escape.
Pay her back for what she has done;
do to her just as she has done,
for she has defied the LORD in her pride, the Holy One of Israel.
30So her young men will fall in her streets,
and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.

31I am against you, Arrogant One,
declares the Lord GOD of Armies,
for your day has arrived, the time for me to punish you.
32The Arrogant One will stumble and fall,
and no one will lift him up.
I will set fire to his towns,
and it will consume everything around him.

The strong Redeemer

33The LORD of Armies says this:
The Israelites are oppressed, and the people of Judah as well.
All their captors hold them tight
and refuse to let them go.
34Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Armies is his name.
He will take up their case and win it,
so that he may bring rest to the earth
and turmoil to those who live in Babylon.
35A sword against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD,
against the people of Babylon,
against her officials and her wise men!
36A sword against the babblers, so that they become fools!
A sword against her warriors, so that they are shattered!
37A sword against her horses and her chariots and against all the mixed peoples in her midst, so that they become like women!
A sword against her treasures, so that they are looted!
38A drought on her waters, so that they dry up!
For it is a land of idols,
and they are crazed by their dreadful images.
39So desert creatures will live there with hyenas,
and ostriches will make their home in her.
She will never be lived in again,
nor settled through all generations.
40As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, declares the LORD,
no one will live there;
no human being will settle in it.
41See, an army is coming from the north;
a mighty nation and many kings
are being roused from the ends of the earth.
42They take hold of bow and spear;
they are cruel and show no mercy.
The noise of them roars like the sea
as they ride on horses,
lined up like a warrior for battle against you, Daughter Babylon.
43The king of Babylon has heard the news of them; his hands hang limp;
distress has gripped him,
pain like a woman in labor.
44Look, an enemy will come up like a lion from the thick brush along the Jordan
against the pastures that never run dry.
In an instant I will chase Babylon’s people from their land,
and I will set over it the one I choose.
For who is like me? Who can call me to account?
What shepherd can stand against me?
45So hear the plan the LORD has made against Babylon,
the purposes he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans:
even the little ones of the flock will be dragged away;
their pasture will be appalled at their fate.
46At the shout, “Babylon is taken!”
the earth will shake,
and a cry will be heard among the nations.
fields.summary: Babylon will fall to a nation from the north, and Israel and Judah will return to seek God.

fields.title: Jeremiah 51
fields.body_html:
A destroying wind

1The LORD says this:
I am stirring up against Babylon
and against the people who live in Leb-qamai
a wind that destroys.
2I will send foreigners to Babylon to winnow her
and to strip her land bare,
for they will come against her from every side on the day of disaster.
3Let the archer bend his bow against her archer,
against the one who stands up in his armor.
Do not spare her young men;
destroy her whole army completely.
4They will fall dead in the land of the Chaldeans,
run through in her streets.
5For Israel and Judah have not been left widowed by their God,
by the LORD of Armies,
though their land is filled with guilt
against the Holy One of Israel.
6Flee from Babylon!
Every one of you, run for your life!
Do not be destroyed when she is punished for her guilt,
for this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance;
he is paying her back what she deserves.
7Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD’s hand,
making the whole earth drunk;
the nations drank her wine,
and so the nations have gone mad.
8Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered.
Wail over her! Bring balm for her wound;
perhaps she can be healed.
9“We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed.
Leave her; let us go, each of us to our own land,
for her judgment reaches up to the heavens;
it rises as high as the clouds.”
10“The LORD has brought our vindication to light.
Come, let us make known in Zion
the work of the LORD our God.”
11Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers!
The LORD has roused the spirit of the Median kings,
because his plan is to destroy Babylon.
This is the LORD’s vengeance,
vengeance for his temple.
12Raise a signal flag against the walls of Babylon!
Strengthen the guard, post the watchmen,
set the ambushes!
For the LORD has planned it, and he has done it:
what he said against the people of Babylon.
13You who live beside many waters,
you with your wealth of treasures,
your end has come; the thread of your life is measured to be cut.
14The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself:
I will fill you with men, as many as locusts,
and they will shout in triumph over you.

15It is he who made the earth by his power,
who set the world firm by his wisdom,
and by his understanding spread out the heavens.
16When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar;
he raises the clouds from the far edges of the earth.
He makes lightning flash with the rain
and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
17Everyone proves senseless and ignorant;
every goldsmith is shamed by his idol,
for the images he casts are a fraud, with no breath in them.
18They are empty breath, a work to be laughed at;
when the time comes to punish them, they will perish.
19The God who is Jacob’s portion is not like these, for he is the one who formed all things,
including the tribe he holds as his own;
the LORD of Armies is his name.

20You are my war club, my weapon of war:
with you I shatter nations;
with you I destroy kingdoms.
21with you I shatter horse and rider;
with you I shatter chariot and driver;
22with you I shatter man and woman;
with you I shatter old and young;
with you I shatter young man and young woman;
23with you I shatter shepherd and flock;
with you I shatter farmer and team of oxen;
with you I shatter governors and officials.
24But I will repay Babylon and all who live in Chaldea
for all the evil they have done in Zion before your eyes, declares the LORD.

25I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD,
you who destroy the whole earth.
I will stretch out my hand against you and roll you down from the cliffs,
and make you a burned-out mountain.
26No one will take a cornerstone from you,
or any stone for a foundation,
for you will be a desolation forever, declares the LORD.
27Raise a signal flag in the land! Sound the ram’s horn among the nations! Set apart nations for holy war against her;
summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz!
Appoint a commander against her;
send up horses like a swarm of bristling locusts!
28Set apart nations for holy war against her: the kings of the Medes,
with their governors and all their officials,
and every land they rule.
29The land trembles and writhes in pain,
for the LORD’s plans against Babylon stand firm:
to make the land of Babylon a wasteland where no one lives.
30Babylon’s warriors have stopped fighting; they stay in their strongholds.
Their strength is gone; they have become like women.
Her houses are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.
31One runner runs to meet another,
one messenger to meet the next,
to tell the king of Babylon
that his city has been taken from end to end.
32The river crossings are seized,
the marshes of reeds are set on fire,
and the soldiers are in panic.

33For the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says this:
